🎙 Maharaj at 40:38 (auto-transcript): “You are going to come to me? Not yet decided. Decided or not? So decided. That is recommended. A chaste lady.”

Kamalakshi Mataji recalls the Puranjana class: Manu-samhita says a king must execute a murderer in this life so he does not suffer for it in the next, but Maharaj had said this does not apply in Kali-yuga. What, then, is the ideal and transparent way to punish a culprit today so that no innocent person is harmed?

🎙 Maharaj at 43:33 (auto-transcript): “I have a question from previous class. that when you are giving class on Puranjan, you told that in Puppet it is mentioned that it is stated in Manu Samhita that it is necessary for a king to execute a murderer for criminal action in this very lifetime, so that next life he…”

children.topic: Arrest and punish — the state's job
children.note:
Maharaj's answer: the best way is to arrest the offender and give the necessary punishment, and that belongs to the government and its agencies, not to us. The trouble is that today they do not arrest — or they arrest, take money and let the culprit go. — “The government can do that.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:59 (auto-transcript): “The best way you can punish, the best way is to arrest them and give them the necessary punishment. They or a passing agency can do like that.”

children.topic: Q3 · What to tell the guru; Krishna's tests vs guru's protection
children.note:
A mataji asks two things. First: Maharaj says be transparent with the guru, but we hold back troubles that seem too small for him, and later they grow big — how do we judge what to share? Second: we are told not to interfere with Krishna's plan, but what if Krishna wants me to face a test while my guru wants to protect me?

🎙 Maharaj at 46:41 (auto-transcript): “Gurudev, I have two questions from the previous classes. So, Gurudev, in one of the classes, you were telling us that we should be transparent with our Guru and we should not complicate the situation. We should let our Guru protect us. so Gurudev sometimes it happens that you…”

children.topic: Tell it while it is small
children.note:
Holding back is simply wrong, Maharaj says; we should tell. A thought kept inside keeps expanding like a clot, and a wound left untreated becomes a big sore. Deal with it while it is small. — “See, it is wrong, it is wrong, we should tell.”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:27 (auto-transcript): “The Guru or the disciple? See, it is wrong, it is wrong, we should tell. If you have a thought, if you don't stick it, it will keep expanding. and the whole clot is the same way if you leave a wound it will expand, become a big sore”

children.topic: Krishna and guru understand each other
children.note:
For a pure devotee there is no tug-of-war: Krishna and the spiritual master know each other. Maharaj says he does not try to arrange his own life; he simply does what comes and learns something from Krishna's arrangement in every situation.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:55 (auto-transcript): “For a pure devotee and for a spiritual devotee and for a spiritual devotee. They know each other. I am not sure what I am doing in my life. It is a good thing. It is a good thing. It is a good thing. It is a good thing. That's why I don't have to do any kind of…”

children.topic: See Krishna's hand, or blame everyone
children.note:
A devotee who keeps the four principles and chants steadily learns to see Krishna's hand in whatever happens. If we do not see that hand, Maharaj warns, we end up accusing everyone around us. — “we will be accusing everyone.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:11 (auto-transcript): “because we are always watching Krishna's hand in our life. If we don't see that, we will be accusing everyone. So, we will try all of you to do this in my life. And we will try to do this in my life. And we will make our own life more and more and more. Most of our lives are…”

children.topic: The fortunate devotee and the snail
children.note:
Most of us see life negatively; a fortunate devotee sees it positively and advances fast. The devotee who is always complaining — why this, why this — moves like a snail. Maharaj acts out the snail, shell on top, taking a year to cross a short distance, and says some of us will take years the same way. — “Why this? Why this? Why?”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:53 (auto-transcript): “Most of our lives are going through this. You seem to grow. Because we don't see anything positive. We always see it negatively. A fortunate devotee. Always see it positively. Degoti with this mentality, they make fast advancement.”

children.topic: Q4 · Knowing the guru by his disciples
children.note:
A devotee quotes Maharaj's saying that one can understand a spiritual master by observing his disciples, and asks: some disciples follow sincerely while others do not — if we watch the non-serious ones we may misjudge the guru. How to know the reality?

🎙 Maharaj at 57:24 (auto-transcript): “Raksha Bhat, what's your question? Dear Ashla Gurudev, please accept my most humble obviously answers. Thank you so much Gurudev for the Nectarian class. Gurudev, I wanted to ask you about something you have often said. that one can understand the spiritual master by…”

Maharaj calls it a general principle: disciples are expected to resemble the guru because the guru's influence shapes them. Still, a disciple's life can differ from his guru's, and Maharaj treats this as a serious matter, citing Lord Balarama's killing of a disciple of Vyasadeva who did not behave as his training required.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:47 (auto-transcript): “That is the general principle. It is expected that the disciples will resemble because the Guru should influence the Lord.”

The root problem today, Maharaj says, is that we are too selfish. To serve the spiritual master nicely and be fully satisfied we need selflessness; self-interested service never satisfies. — “because we are too selfish.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:58 (auto-transcript): “But these days, because we are too selfish. We are good to serve the spiritual master nicely. To be full satisfied. We must be selfish. Selflessness”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 07 · Who was Vallabha Acharya?

nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.55–69 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Mahaprabhu assures Rupa Gosvami that Sanatana is already free, settles at Prayaga, and is visited by the scholar Vallabha Bhatta. Maharaj uses Prabhupada's long purport on Vallabha's life to warn against seeking position in Krishna consciousness, and in the Q&A explains why pure devotees withhold prema from the unready and why the Lord hid his ecstasy before Vallabha while using Rupa's humility to teach him. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Maharaj resumes the chapter in which Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu instructs Srila Rupa Gosvami. Today's verses take the story from Rupa's arrival at Prayaga to the meeting with Vallabha Bhatta, read with Hindi translation.
Rupa Gosvami tells the Lord that his brother Sanatana lies arrested by Hussain Shah's government; Mahaprabhu answers at once that Sanatana has been released and will soon come to him.
A brahmana invites Mahaprabhu to lunch and Balabhadra Bhattacarya invites the two brothers; they receive the remnants from the Lord's own plate.
The Lord stays beside the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, and Rupa Gosvami with his brother Sri Vallabha (Anupama) take a place nearby.

The verse introduces Vallabha Bhatta, who was living at Adaila village and came to see Mahaprabhu when he heard of his arrival. Prabhupada's purport tells his whole story, which Maharaj reads first in Hindi and then in English.

children.topic: Devoted at first, then he left
children.note:
A great scholar of Vaishnavism, Vallabha was in the beginning very attached to Mahaprabhu. Feeling he did not receive the respect he expected, he later joined the Vishnu Swami line and became its acarya.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:28 (auto-transcript): “Vallabha Bhatta was a great learned scholar of Vaishnavaism. In the beginning, he was very much devoted to Sri Tithanya Mahabharata. But since he taught that he could not receive proper respect from him, he later joined the Vishnu Swami sect and became the acharya of that sect.”

children.topic: He wanted to be another Mahaprabhu
children.note:
Maharaj's reading of the story: Vallabha followed the Lord in order to be recognised, to become a second Caitanya Mahaprabhu. The original did not accept this, so he went away and took over another sampradaya.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:39 (auto-transcript): “Then the scholar, Vaishnava Izu, was following Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu not following Chaitanya Mahaprabhu he is not following Chaitanya Mahaprabhu he came to be recognized and become another Chaitanya Mahaprabhu But the original Chaitanya Mahapura did not accept that before…”

Looking for position and recognition, and taking to Krishna consciousness in order to make a business of it — Maharaj calls this dangerous. The warning is for us, not only for history. — “This is dangerous.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:41 (auto-transcript): “this is what, this is what, looking for position, want recognition, I couldn't get from Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, so he left, business, making business, taking to Krishna consciousness”

The sampradaya he led has great influence around Gokul, Vrindavan and Bombay. He wrote the Subodhini commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam, the Anubhasya on Vedanta-sutra and sixteen short works called Sodasa-grantha; his village of Adaila still has a Vishnu temple of his line.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:39 (auto-transcript): “This Sampradaya has been, has had great influence in Brindavan, near Gokul, and in Bombay. Vallabha Bhatta wrote many books, including a common tree on Simad Bhagavatam called Subodini Tika, and wrote the Vedanta Sutra in the form of Anubhashya. He also wrote a combination of…”

Maharaj continues Prabhupada's account of Vallabha's origins: a brahmana family from a village in southern India near the Nidadavolu station, one of the five brahmana communities of Andhra. He pauses the reading to joke, to ask the room questions, and to point to places nearby.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:05 (auto-transcript): “Vallabha Bhatta was originally from a place in southern India called, there is a railway station there called Nidada. Sixteen miles from that station is a village called Kankadaba. and the Brahmana named Lakshmana used to live there, and Vallabha Bhatta was his son.”

The purport gives different versions — birth in 1478, or in 1400, at Kankadaba, at Champakaranya, or near Rajim in Madhya Pradesh. Asked which is correct, Maharaj says all of them are, and moves on.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:53 (auto-transcript): “There are five sections of the Brahmana community of Andhra Pradesh, as Bela Nati, Vegi Nati, Buraki Nati, Telugu Nati, and Kassala Nati. Out of these five Brahminical communities, Vallabha Acharya took his birth in the community of Bela Nati in the year 14 Zakapta era, 1478 A.D.”

children.topic: A father who took sannyasa, then returned
children.note:
One account says Vallabha's father took sannyasa before the boy's birth and came back home to accept him as his son. Maharaj stops and makes the room laugh over what kind of sannyasa this was.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:52 (auto-transcript): “How did he? The household again or what? Not birth. According to some people, Valabha Bhattacharya's father took sannyas before Valabha's birth”

After eleven years of study at Varanasi he returned home, enlightened Krishnadeva, grandson of King Bukka, at Vidyanagara on the Tungabhadra, toured India three times for six years each, and married at thirty within his own community.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:40 (auto-transcript): “After studying for 11 years at Varanasi, Balabacharya returned home. On his return, he heard that his father had departed from the material world, keeping his brother and mother at home. He went to the banks of the river Tunga to a village called Vidyanagara, where he…”

children.topic: Have you seen his deity at Govardhan?
children.note:
The purport says he installed a deity near Govardhan. Maharaj turns to the audience — it is close to here; have you seen it? A devotee explains in Hindi where the deity is kept.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:08 (auto-transcript): “He is near Gauravadan here. He established a deity in the valley. Have you seen it? Have you seen the deity? What have you seen? Kishini Vigra Rekha Govardhan Me, Balabachar Ji Ka, Afsarakund Ke Paaf Jhansai Murutein, Ander Atein, Vahin Parai.”

Vallabha finally settled at Adaila across the Yamuna from Prayaga, had two sons, Gopinatha and Vitthalesvara, took the renounced order in old age and passed away at Varanasi in 1530.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:11 (auto-transcript): “Balabacharya had two sons, Gopinath and Baita Leshwar. And in his old age, he accepted the renounced order in 1452 Sakavda area. 1530 AD, he passed away from the material world at Paranasi. His book, known as Sodasa Grant, and his commentaries on the Vedanta Sutra, Anubhashya…”
Vallabha Bhatta offers obeisances, the Lord embraces him and they speak of Krishna. These verses describe how Mahaprabhu is moved by the talk but restrains himself before his visitor.

Feeling shy before Vallabha, the Lord holds back his feelings externally, yet the ecstatic love cannot be fully checked and Vallabha is astonished to notice it.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:30 (auto-transcript): “Shri Chacha Mahaprabhu felt great aesthetic love when they began discussing Krishna. But the Lord checked his feelings because he felt shy before Vala Bapata. Although the Lord restrained himself externally,”
Vallabha invites the Lord for lunch and Mahaprabhu introduces the brothers Rupa and Vallabha (Anupama). They offer obeisances from the ground with great humility.

When Vallabha Bhatta walks toward them the brothers run further off, Rupa Gosvami calling himself untouchable and most sinful. Vallabha is surprised; the Lord is delighted and begins to describe Rupa to him.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:36 (auto-transcript): “When Balabha Bhattacharya walked toward them, they ran away to a more distant place, Rupa Goswami said, I am untouchable and most sinful, please do not touch me. Bhalla Bhattacharya was very much surprised at this.”
Mahaprabhu tells Vallabha, a Vedic ritualist of aristocratic birth, not to touch Rupa because he is of low caste. The purport explains the brahminical pride the Lord is pointing at.

Prabhupada describes how Mahaprabhu began a revolution against caste pride by inaugurating the chanting of Hare Krishna, which purifies anyone regardless of birth, and hints to Vallabha not to neglect one who chants.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:41 (auto-transcript): “Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu actually started the revolution against this brahmanical system by inaugurating the chanting of the Hare Krishna mantra. But this chanting, one can be delivered regardless of curse, greed, color, or social position. Whoever chants the Hare Krishna…”

Rupa Gosvami came from an aristocratic brahmana family but was excommunicated for serving the Muslim Nawab; the Lord accepted him for his devotion. Vallabha knew all this, yet still felt his own prestige.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:40 (auto-transcript): “Actually, Rupaku Swami did not belong to a lower caste. He was from a highly aristocratic Brahmana family. But due to his association with the Muslim Nawab, he was considered foreign and was excommunicated from Brahmana society. However, due to his advanced devotional…”

The purport notes that the head of the Vallabha sampradaya in Bombay in Prabhupada's time, Dikshit Maharaj, was a friendly life member who praised the Hare Krishna movement and accepted its members as genuine Vaishnavas.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:30 (auto-transcript): “The present head of the Balabha Bhattacharya, Sampradaya of Bambi, is named Dikshita Maharao. He's very friendly to our movement. And whenever we meet him, this learned Brahmana scholar highly presses the activities of the Herakasya movement. He's a life member of our…”

Two questions: one on whether pure devotees 'cheat' duplicitous disciples, and one on why the Lord gave Vallabha his association at all.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:16 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna. Comment? Kishira Kautipari, Prashna. Hare Krishna, Sri Gurudev. Hare Krishna. Thank you. My question is to take Indega to Mohani class. I asked this question to you two years back, but I was not so clear that time. So, you are saying how pure devotee they are…”

children.topic: Q1 · Pure devotees cheat the duplicitous — what hope for us?
children.note:
A devotee recalls Maharaj saying pure devotees are like a two-edged sword, cheating disciples who are duplicitous. If we are not grossly after position but still cannot follow, are we also being cheated? Then what is our hope?

🎙 Maharaj at 37:43 (auto-transcript): “My question is to take Indega to Mohani class. I asked this question to you two years back, but I was not so clear that time. So, you are saying how pure devotee they are like two-edged swords. They are like two-edged sword. So, they cheat those duplicitous disciples. So, I…”

children.topic: I only repeat what I heard
children.note:
Maharaj answers that the statement is not his own; he repeats what he heard from his predecessors, and repeating is the principle of our system. Why then challenge him for it? — “Our principle is to repeat.”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:57 (auto-transcript): “I think that you should ask a question, who has told you, Parambhutu Gargoyin, Sai Mahārāj. For him, and I repeat it, it was my fault. I have heard him, and he has blown away my mind. This is our system, it is to repeat. Our principle is to repeat. I did. I did. So I have…”

Many come to the movement wanting position. What a person is not ready for will not be good for him, so it has to come step by step.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:48 (auto-transcript): “Many people, movement, give your possessions, therefore, to do something. The position is good for them.”

Ours is a system of salvage — making the best use of a bad bargain. Chances are given, but a pure devotee will not hand bhakti or prema to one who is still on a lower platform, just as we do not give the holy name to the faithless. Such people stay, do service and are promoted in time.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:01 (auto-transcript): “Our system is a salvage system, salvationism, making best use of a bad baguette. So, chances are given. Those who are still on that platform, pure devotee will not give them bhakti. Will not give.”

children.topic: Punishment comes from their own desire
children.note:
The sincere, even with material desires, receive blessing and go on. The crooked and hard-hearted are pushed down by the very position they wanted — but that is their desire, not the pure devotee's. The pure devotee is merciful; even his punishment is mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:05 (auto-transcript): “But those who are really crooked, those who are hard-hearted, the position still will not help them. It will push them down. But that is their desire. It is not pure devotees' desire They are imposed on them. The pure devotee is messy. Even punishment is messy. Does it make…”

children.topic: Weak is not the same as unready
children.note:
Not following instructions means one is not ready; a weak person who is ready can be helped. Maharaj's picture: someone offers you food, you say you are too weak, so he puts it in your mouth — will he chew and swallow for you too? A mother does that for an infant, not for a grown child. We must do our own part. — “Someone is giving you something, at least you should take it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:18 (auto-transcript): “Not being able to follow instructions means one is not ready. If one is ready,”

children.topic: Q2 · Why did the Lord still associate with Vallabha?
children.note:
If Vallabha wanted to become another Mahaprabhu and the Lord was not interested in him, why do we see Mahaprabhu giving him his association here? Had Vallabha's intention changed?

🎙 Maharaj at 49:25 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj, thank you so much for the wonderful class. Maharaj, you mentioned that Vallabha Bhatt wanted to become Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. So Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was not interested in him. But later on we see that Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is giving his association to…”

Before Rupa Gosvami the Lord never covers his ecstasy; it flows freely. Here he holds it in because Vallabha is an outsider — yet Mahaprabhu is there to help him and raise his standard. — “He would flow and overflow.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:23 (auto-transcript): “Chaitanya Mahaprabhu would not cover his ecstasy in the presence of Rupa Goswami, he would not. He would flow and overflow. He is holding it. Why? He is an outsider. Chetanamu is there to help him.”

children.topic: Rupa and Anupama as the lesson
children.note:
The Lord uses the two brothers to teach the proud brahmana: you are exalted, he is untouchable, don't touch him. The contrast is meant to expose Vallabha's contaminated pride.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:12 (auto-transcript): “He is using Rupa Goswami and Anupam to teach him a lesson. You are a Brahmana. Means what? Follow his pride. Contaminated. You are exalted. The Lord is there to help him. To raise his standard.”

Vallabha noticed that the 'untouchable' brothers' tongues never left the Hare Krishna mantra. That was the lesson Mahaprabhu intended, and he received it.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:32 (auto-transcript): “Rupa Goswami's tongue. They constantly channeled a Christian mantra. They never leave their tongue. Either I wake up. So Allah ever noticed it. So he said, The lesson Chaitanya Mahabrabhu wanted to teach, he got it. Because their tongue is constantly,”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 08 · Who is a Qualified Brahmana?

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · Who is a Qualified Brahmana?
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.70–72 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Vallabha Bhattacarya hears Rupa and Anupama chanting constantly and declares that such people cannot be untouchable — they are most exalted. Maharaj asks who is really a brahmana: birth gives only the name, quality gives the position, and the chanter of the holy name has already done everything the Vedas prescribe. Two stories — Srivasa Pandit framed by an envious neighbour, and Haridasa Thakura cursed by a proud brahmana — show what pride of birth does, and why real repentance means going back to the person one has offended. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse describes Vallabha Bhattacarya hearing the two brothers chant Krishna's name without a break and grasping what Caitanya Mahaprabhu was indicating by it. The reading is given in English and Hindi.

Vallabha Bhattacarya, an authority on brahminical culture, concludes that people who constantly chant the holy name cannot be untouchable; they are the most exalted. Maharaj uses Prabhupada's purport about proud brahmanas who still do not accept Western devotees.

Maharaj recalls brahmanas who came to the temple, accepted prasadam and wanted to carry it away. Prabhupada insisted again and again that they eat it on the spot, because the wish to take it away showed they still thought the devotees untouchable. — “Take prasadam here.”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:10 (auto-transcript): “He observed that some of the brahmanas, when they came, Prabhupada always insisted that this was self-prasad. So they would take and take it away. So Prabhupada was insisting. Take prasadam here. Insisted, so take prasadam here.”

Maharaj turns the word upside down: the man free from illicit sex, gambling, intoxication and meat, chanting Hare Krishna all day, is counted unqualified, while one who keeps none of these and never chants is counted qualified by birth. Even in Vrindavan this birth consideration persists.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:46 (auto-transcript): “One who is free from illicit sex, gamboli, deducation, flesh-eating, and is constantly chanting Hare Krishna, is not qualified. One who is not keeping any of these principles, he is not chanting, he is qualified. But he is here in Vrindavan,”

Maharaj acts out Rupa Gosvami and Anupama backing away when Vallabha wanted to touch them, as if to say they were not fit to be touched. Vallabha looked at them and said the opposite: one who chants Krishna's name constantly cannot be untouchable.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:04 (auto-transcript): “So Rupa Goswami and Anupam, they ran all the way about the church. No, don't touch us. Don't touch us. We are exalted Brahman. don't worry, we are exalted brahman. But he looked at them. One who is constantly chanting the holy name of Krishna.”

children.topic: 19.72 — The dog-eater who chants is worshipable
children.note: Vallabha recites Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.33.7, Devahuti's words to Kapila: a person born among dog-eaters becomes worshipable when the holy name is on his tongue, because he has already done all that the Vedas prescribe.

Maharaj asks who these great souls are and answers from the verse: the holy name is dancing on their tongue. He quotes Prabhupada — you are chanting in the streets, Krishna is dancing on the devotees' tongues; how can such a person be untouchable?

🎙 Maharaj at 12:38 (auto-transcript): “Who is people? Why? Such who are great, what do they say? Namah tu biam. A holy name is dancing on their tongue. Aapka naam. Mata bol lehi hain Kapil deo ko. the holy name Srila Prabhupada said in the streets you are chanting Krishna dancing on the tongue of devotees in the…”

The constant chanter is understood to have bathed in all the holy rivers, performed every sacrifice in the scriptures over many lifetimes and visited all the holy places. There is nothing left for him to do but go on chanting.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:51 (auto-transcript): “who is constantly chanting a holy name has in their previous life built in all the holy rivers in the world. Has performed all the jaguars in the scripture for many lifetimes. Has visited the holy places around the world. So he has filled with everything Now, the only thing…”

children.topic: Promoted to the rank of Arya
children.note:
Such a person is not merely touchable but worshipable, because the holy name of Krishna has purified him. Birth calculation has no say over this promotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:49 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, he has been promoted to the cycle of Arya. Similarist person, not untouchable, is touchable, worshipable, because I've been purified by the Holy Name of Krishna. One is born in the Brahmana family.”

Maharaj sets out the principle of the class: birth in a brahmana family without brahminical qualities does not make a brahmana. Everything in this world and beyond is named according to the quality it possesses.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:25 (auto-transcript): “One is born in the Brahmana family. does not have brahmanical qualities. He is not a brahmana. A best friend of brahman. Not a brahman, but a friend. Unqualified friend. because they have some relationship with Brahmana.”

One born in the family but without the qualities is called a friend of the brahmanas, not a brahmana — an unqualified relative who happens to have a relationship with them.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:46 (auto-transcript): “He is not a brahmana. A best friend of brahman. Not a brahman, but a friend. Unqualified friend. because they have some relationship with Brahmana. Literally speaking,”

If your father is an astronaut, are you an astronaut? Maharaj says the son still has to go to school to become qualified. The same applies to the brahmana's son.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:32 (auto-transcript): “if you are astronaut, astronaut, yes, someone is also an astronaut, He has to go to school if he wants, he has to go to school to be qualified. we have seen worshipping Durga”

children.topic: A brahmana worships Brahman, not Durga
children.note:
Brahmana means one who sees Brahman. Worship of Durga with flesh to get material facilities is the sudra's way; a brahmana does not look for material facilities at all. Yet Maharaj has seen many so-called brahmanas doing exactly this. — “a Brahmana does not look for material facilities”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:43 (auto-transcript): “Brahmana worship Brahman Brahman Brahman Brahman that's the meaning Brahmana one who is seeing Brahman not Durga Durga worshiper means a sudra worshipping Durga offering flesh to Durga to get material facilities a Brahmana does not look for material facilities You only look…”

Here in Vrindavan, Krishna told his father which brahmanas are qualified: those who never lie, are not greedy for others' property and are satisfied with what they have. Their blessings work automatically; a greedy brahmana's blessing has no effect, because the quality is missing.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:36 (auto-transcript): “Here in Vrindavan, when Krishna was physically present, Krishna told his father, God qualifies Brahmanas who never tell lies. Not interested in someone's property, not greedy, satisfied with what he has. Krishna said, such brahmanas, their benediction works automatically,…”

children.topic: Srivasa Pandit framed by his neighbour
children.note:
A brahmana who worshipped Durga wanted to disgrace Srivasa Pandit, whose house rang with the holy name day and night. At night he placed wine, flesh and other articles of goddess worship at Srivasa's door and left.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:36 (auto-transcript): “Srivast Pandit brought wine, flesh, other substances worshiping Durga. And placed it in Srivast Pandit's house. He left. He did that in the night.”

Maharaj asks the room what Srivasa should do on opening the door. Clean it quickly before anyone sees? Srivasa did the opposite: he called the neighbours and announced, you all think I am a devotee — see what I do every night; do not consider me a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:15 (auto-transcript): “What did he do? What did he do? What would he do? Clean it before someone else sees it.”

Why could he behave like that? Because he had full confidence in Krishna consciousness and was not afraid of what people might say about him. The neighbours saw at once who had done it. — “He's not worried what people say about him.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:27 (auto-transcript): “Shiva has confidence in Krishna. He's not worried what people say about him. He's not afraid about what people say. He's confident. Krishna consciousness. So as soon as people came and saw that,”

The offender got white leprosy that ate his body. Crying, he came to Caitanya Mahaprabhu as the saviour of the most fallen. The Lord became furious: your suffering has not started yet, this is only the introduction; nobody can save you — and chased him away.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:24 (auto-transcript): “He got white leprosy. was crying. The Loprosi was eating his body. Was crying. He went to meet Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. You are the savior of the most fallen. I am very, very fallen. Please help me. I'm suffering hearing from him since then Mahapu became very furious your…”

children.topic: Go back to the one you offended
children.note:
Even so the man kept begging: if you do not deliver me, who will? Maharaj calls this a good attitude, arrived at only after destroying himself. Finally he was told: if you want to be saved, go to Srivasa Pandit; if he forgives you, you are free.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:16 (auto-transcript): “Shri Vash Thakur told him if you want to save yourself go back to Shri Vash Pondit if he forgive you then you are free. What is the lesson? We have a Christian background, very dirty background. Every Saturday,”

Maharaj draws the lesson from his own Christian upbringing: Saturday confession to the reverend father, a small penance such as cutting grass at the mission school, Sunday as a holy man — and Monday back to the same thing. He calls this cheating; Mahaprabhu did not do it.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:35 (auto-transcript): “What is the lesson? We have a Christian background, very dirty background. Every Saturday, we go to Reverend Father and confessed. And he would say, go and do this service. You are free.”

I stole someone's eyeglasses and confess it to you, you set me a penance and say I am free — what have you done? You have encouraged me to steal again and come back to confess. Maharaj calls the arrangement dangerous. — “You are encouraging me to continue stealing.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:09 (auto-transcript): “I stole the eyeglass I'm going to confess to you Please forgive me. I stole someone's eyeglass. I'm sorry. Please forgive me. Okay, cut this place. You are free. What have you done? You are encouraging me to continue stealing. And come and confess. It's dangerous, it's dangerous.”

Ritual atonement has no power to remove the seed of sinful life; the holy name does. True repentance can burn karma, and repentance is true only when we do not repeat the act. The person we offended is the person we must beg. — “Prayashita has no potency to remove the seed of sinful life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:04 (auto-transcript): “Prayashita has no potency to remove the seed of sinful life. The holy name has the potency to uproot the seed of sin. True repentance has the potency to ban our karma. It must be true repentance. And repentance means we don't repeat it.”

A disciple once came asking Maharaj to forgive him, insisting Guru Dev knows everything. Maharaj replied that he did not know and asked him to say what he had done — without confession there is no freedom. All our acaryas confessed openly; Maharaj's favourite prayer says there is no sin I have not committed a million times, who can free me but you? The acarya has no sin; he is teaching us. — “Confession is necessary.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:42 (auto-transcript): “one time a devotee came to me and said forgive me forgive you for what you know everything Guru Dev you know everything forgive you he know me please forgive me I said I don't know you please tell me what am I doing if you don't confess you will not be freed.”

children.topic: Haridasa Thakura and the proud brahmana
children.note:
The brahmana who framed Srivasa was qualified by birth to enter Jagannatha Puri, while Prabhupada's Western disciples are not — Maharaj asks whether that is qualification. He then tells of another brahmana who challenged Haridasa Thakura: which scripture says one should chant the holy name loudly?

🎙 Maharaj at 37:36 (auto-transcript): “So this person who did this is a brahmana. But he was being durga. Yet he is qualified to enter Jagannathpuri. Is he not? You are not qualified. But I'm qualified to enter there because I took birth here. No.”

children.topic: Not a brahmana, yet he quotes scripture
children.note:
Haridasa Thakura answered humbly that he only repeats what he has heard from exalted persons like them, then quoted the Bhagavatam and the Puranas. Maharaj asks: was Haridasa a brahmana by birth? No. Was his challenger a brahmana by qualification? No. Haridasa had the qualification and could speak from scripture.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:05 (auto-transcript): “I don't know any way but I am saying what I have from exalted personalities like you what I have from you I am repeating Haridash Thakura he quoted come to 10 chapter 34 then come to Bagotam did he study Bagotam? Haridash Thakura did he study Bagotam? how did he know? Haritha…”

Loud chanting is said to be thousands of times superior to soft chanting because the living entities who cannot chant still hear it; it is magnanimous, benefiting everyone. Soft chanting, Maharaj says, is for oneself.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:32 (auto-transcript): “that chanting the name loudly is thousands of times superior thousands of times superior to a soft chanting because when we chant loud the entities who cannot they will hear magnanimous benefiting benefiting everyone”

children.topic: The curse falls back on the curser
children.note:
The brahmana cursed Haridasa, who simply replied, as you like. Soon leprosy took the proud man's handsome nose and his fingers, while Haridasa went on chanting Hare Krishna. Maharaj's warning: look carefully before you touch a pure devotee; one who offends a constant chanter is tortured.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:30 (auto-transcript): “Ramana said if he did not do what I'm saying I curse you Haradas say as you like no problem not quite long his standing His nose was a handsome boy, very handsome, his nose was standing. Leprosy cut it off.”

Three devotees ask about loud and soft chanting, self-criticism versus confession, and the hint Vallabha Bhattacarya understood in verse 70.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:23 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Shriya Gurudev, please accept my obeisances. Thank you. Shriya Gurudev, I have two questions. One, I wanted to know that advanced devotees or pure devotees, we mostly externally see that they are chanting softly. So how do we understand the loud chanting, is it…”

children.topic: Q1 · Pure devotees chant softly — why?
children.note:
We see advanced devotees chanting japa softly, yet the verse praises loud chanting. Is it kirtan that is meant, or loud japa? And is the soft chanter perhaps vibrating fully within?

🎙 Maharaj at 47:34 (auto-transcript): “Shriya Gurudev, I have two questions. One, I wanted to know that advanced devotees or pure devotees, we mostly externally see that they are chanting softly. So how do we understand the loud chanting, is it the kirtan or is it loud japa that is being referred to over here and…”

Maharaj answers that Haridasa Thakura chanted in three styles — a hundred thousand within the mind, a hundred thousand softly and a hundred thousand aloud. Kirtan is loud chanting too.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:44 (auto-transcript): “Shri La Haridash Thakura used to chant three styles of chant. Shri La Haridash Thakura used to chant three styles. One is inside. Hundred. Hundred outside, soft.”

children.topic: Even soft chanting affects by sight
children.note:
A pure devotee's soft chanting still works: whoever sees him is affected, and a fortunate person hears him even when he is quiet.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:53 (auto-transcript): “By seeing him, he'll be affected. By seeing him, he'll be affected. He has an effect. And if one is fortunate, he will hear, even though he's soft, he will hear. Shuddha Bhaktika. That is the second one. The second one is Goethe, morning we were hearing that”

Our acaryas, Bhaktivinoda Thakura especially, speak openly about their faults; yet being too critical of oneself is said to be an offence. Where is the line between seeing faults in ourselves and the acaryas' positive confession?

🎙 Maharaj at 50:34 (auto-transcript): “The second one is Goethe, morning we were hearing that we should dissociate the mind with all the material activities and then only this third question had come that all our acharyas, Bhakti not Thakul specifically mentioned today, they are very confessional and they are…”

children.topic: Too humble to serve is also an offence
children.note:
Maharaj first names the false humility: I am not this, I am not that, so I do nothing — that is aparadha, not humility.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:26 (auto-transcript): “If one is too humble to do service, it's an apparate, you're not humility. So if one is not this, and not this, and not this, and do nothing, it's an apparate. It is a purification to examine ourselves.”

Looking into our own heart is itself purifying and cannot be skipped; otherwise we live in self-deceit, imagining we are what we are not. Putting on the light in the room of consciousness means looking at ourselves instead of cataloguing everyone else's faults. — “It is a purification to examine ourselves.”

🎙 Maharaj at 53:07 (auto-transcript): “It is a purification to examine ourselves. It is compulsory for us to do that. Otherwise, we will be fully engaged in self-deceit. What we are not. check where we are in our Christian consciousness.”

We cannot give what we do not have. Loving myself means no illicit sex, gambling, intoxication or flesh and at least sixteen rounds; then I love you by reminding you to do the same. Seeing our faults should only lead us to improve.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:06 (auto-transcript): “Bhakti Maharaj said we should love ourselves if we don't love ourselves we cannot love somebody else because why will you give something we don't have we give what we have if I love myself no illicit sex no gambling no intoxication no flesh eating minimum 16 rounds means I…”

To the follow-up — what is this self we love? — Maharaj says purification is of the body and its coverings, never of the soul, which is eternally pure; as the anarthas go, the soul is fully manifest. He has Bhagavad-gita 13.32 read aloud: the soul is beyond the three modes and is not entangled.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:23 (auto-transcript): “Purification is not the soul, purification is the body, the soul is eternally pure. The purification is the body.”

children.topic: Q3 · What was the hint in 19.70?
children.note:
What indication did Caitanya Mahaprabhu give that Vallabha Bhattacarya understood?

🎙 Maharaj at 61:02 (auto-transcript): “I just have two small questions. So, first one is that, in the verse 70, we saw that it said that Valdavacharya understood the indication of Lord Chaitanya Mahabrabhu. Mahaprabhu. What is the indication of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu here? What is the indication here which Lord…”

The hint: one who chants the holy name cannot be untouchable, and a pure devotee must not be treated as a sudra. Once one is a pure devotee, sudra, vaisya, ksatriya, brahmana, sannyasi, guru — all labels end. Vallabha was fortunate to receive the message through the Lord's behaviour and respond to it. — “All designations finished.”

🎙 Maharaj at 61:52 (auto-transcript): “One who is chanting the Holy Land cannot be untouchable. . One should not be poor to be a and consider a sutra who is a pure devotee to be a sutra. . When one has become a pure devotee, he's no more”

Academic qualification, scholarship and high position have no place in pure Krishna consciousness. Maharaj tells of a sweet-rice competition he held in Brazil on the last day of Kartik: a professional restaurant cook entered, the entries were unnamed, and the winner was a poor newcomer eager to become a pure devotee. Krishna tastes the consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:53 (auto-transcript): “Academic qualification Scholarship And high position has no place in pure Krishna consciousness. So Krishna accepts our love, our sacrifice, not our expertise. I am very expert. It doesn't exist here.”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 09 · Anyone Can Be Transformed

nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.73–76 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Mahaprabhu, pleased with Vallabha Bhatta, quotes scripture on the real position of a devotee: devotion, not birth or learning, makes a brahmana. Maharaj teaches that being a devotee is not external — Dhruva, Gajendra and we ourselves came to Krishna with mixed motives and were transformed — and tells how Narottama dasa Thakura converted two boys sent to worship Durga. In the question time he insists that a pure devotee never suffers, with the Pandavas, Bhakti Tirtha Swami and Jayapataka Swami as his examples. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse describes Mahaprabhu's delight on hearing Vallabha Bhattacarya quote scripture about the position of a devotee, and how he himself, in ecstatic love, begins quoting many verses. The class is read in Vrindavan with Hindi translation.

The first verse Mahaprabhu quotes, from the Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya: it is about the person whose devotional service has given him the real qualities of a brahmana, however low his birth, as against the learned atheist whom the wise do not recognise.

The second quotation: what noble family, Vedic learning, austerity and mantra-chanting amount to when there is no devotion to the Lord. Maharaj notes that the same verse is quoted again elsewhere in the book.
Vallabha Bhattacarya is struck by the Lord's ecstatic symptoms, his grasp of the essence of devotional service, and his beauty and influence.

Maharaj reads a long purport built around Narottama dasa Thakura, who was born in a non-brahmana family yet initiated brahmanas, and the scriptural support for a devotee's standing above caste. The reading runs for about twenty minutes before the teaching begins.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:43 (auto-transcript): “Yes, we want to continue on this topic, Hari Bhakti Shudodaya, Hari Bhakti Shudodaya se liya gaya hai, okay, this is already squatted here, this image is squatted here, this image is squatted here, this image is squatted here, the same verse,”

The purport recounts that so-called brahmanas — worshipping Durga and eating meat — were angry to see Narottama dasa Thakura give initiation to brahmanas and set out to challenge him.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:17 (auto-transcript): “Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu sent him to materially, materially, materially low class family. So, ordinary people did not recognize him. They were angry.”

children.topic: Ganga Narayana told to stop wasting time
children.note:
The scholar Ganga Narayana Cakravarti is told by Narottama dasa Thakura that his learning is a waste of life unless he gives it to Krishna; the discussion continues with quotations on Vaisnava dharma.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:05 (auto-transcript): “Narottam Dashthakur Ganga Narayan is a big scholar. Narottamda said, Kura, you are wasting your time. Narottamda Kura is telling him, you are wasting your time. You should give your life to Krishna. Yes. And then we continue. We continue the discussion.”

children.topic: Only a Vaisnava can be guru
children.note:
The reading covers the ranking of worshippers — Ganapati, the sun god, Shiva and Durga, and above all Vishnu — the instruction to reject a non-Vaisnava guru and be initiated again, and the four sampradayas that purify Kali-yuga.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:32 (auto-transcript): “Never accept a non-vaiṣṇava as guru If you happen to have sought a spiritual master Reject him and accept a vaiṣṇava guru All the mantras chanted by the worshippers of Ganapati.”

children.topic: A devotee is never a sudra
children.note:
From Hari-bhakti-vilasa and other sastra: a devotee of Krishna, whatever his birth, is counted among the Bhagavatas, while a brahmana, kshatriya or vaisya without devotion is to be seen as a sudra.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:22 (auto-transcript): “A devotee of Krishna is never a sudra, but a Brahmana who has no devotion for Lord Krishna is lower than a sudra. This is stated in the sastra. A devotee should never be considered a sudra.”

The purport's image for initiation: as mercury turns bell metal into gold, so a disciple initiated by a bona fide guru at once attains the position of a brahmana — the reason Narottama dasa Thakura, born in a kayastha family, cannot be called a sudra.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:51 (auto-transcript): “A bell meter can be turned into when treated with mercury. A disciple initiated by a bona fide guru,”

children.topic: To be a devotee is not external
children.note:
Maharaj's first point: once the heart is given to Krishna through proper training from a bona fide spiritual master, external considerations of birth and status have no value. He checks with the room — is it not? — “To be a devotee is not an external thing.”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:24 (auto-transcript): “To be a devotee is not an external thing. If the heart is given to Krishna, by proper training, proper training means from a bona fide spiritual master the external considerations has no value is it not? is it not? how did”

How did Dhruva Maharaja become a pure devotee? Maharaj reminds us that his starting motive was not to go back to Godhead but a material desire — not pure at all — and yet he was transformed.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:08 (auto-transcript): “how did Dvamaharayas become a beauty How did he become a pure beauty? What was his motivation? He had desire. Not to go to Godhead. He wanted material desires. Is it not?”

Gajendra turned to Krishna only because he was in distress. Maharaj asks what the end was: the Lord did not send him a separate plane like other souls returning to Godhead but seated him on his own carrier and they went together. — “No. Krishna did not give Gajendra a separate airplane.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:59 (auto-transcript): “Gajendra. How did he become a devotee? He was in distress. He was in distress. But what was the end? Gajendra. You will see that People go to Godhead by using a plane to go to Godhead. Gajendra, how did he go?”

children.topic: Do not judge devotees by their past
children.note:
Maharaj says he knows how many of us came: poor, about to die, the hospital could not cure us. A man who was poor and is now rich says, yes, but then what — I am richer than you now. We should see devotees the same way: a sudra who has become a pure devotee is no longer a sudra. — “If a poor person becomes rich, will you remember his poverty position?”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:06 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, if you look at I know how you came to Krishna. I know how you were Krishna. Everybody poor. You were very about to die. Hospital couldn't kill you. That's why you came to Krishna. What is that? It's a product. Affected. You don't look at devotees.”

children.topic: Proper training under a bona fide guru
children.note:
The heart is given to Krishna by training, and training means from a bona fide spiritual master. This is what carries weight, not the family one was born in.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:40 (auto-transcript): “by proper training, proper training means from a bona fide spiritual master the external considerations has no value is it not? is it not? how did Dvamaharayas become a beauty How did he become a pure beauty?”

Maharaj tells how Narottama dasa Thakura met two boys carrying goods for their master's Durga worship. Sit down, he said — this is dangerous, animals are being killed; have you checked with Durga whether she likes it? They had not; they abandoned the errand and became devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:30 (auto-transcript): “One day, Nautam Dasukhara saw two boys, they were carrying goods. So he asked, where are you taking this thing for? Master is going to worship Durga with these goods. That's what I said, sit down, sit down, this activity is very dangerous, we are killing”

The master, having lost two disciples and his puja, plotted against Narottama dasa Thakura and failed. Why? Because Krishna protects his devotees. In the end the master himself took initiation from him. — “Devotees are fully protected by Lord Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:18 (auto-transcript): “He didn't succeed. Why? Devotees are fully protected by Lord Krishna. At the end, they took initiation from Narottam Dasakura. That is the beauty of pure Krishna consciousness. Anyone can be transformed. Anyone will be transformed, if you take association with devotees, if…”

This is the beauty of pure Krishna consciousness: anyone, whatever their start, is transformed when they take the association of devotees. — “Anyone can be transformed.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:43 (auto-transcript): “Anyone can be transformed. Anyone will be transformed, if you take association with devotees, if you take association with devotees, we will be transformed. Bhagavan Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, They will follow Bhattacharya. According to scripture. Persons who are constantly…”

Mahaprabhu tells the Bhattacarya, following scripture, that those who constantly chant the Hare Krishna mantra from the heart cannot be untouchable — rather, touching them purifies.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:13 (auto-transcript): “According to scripture. Persons who are constantly chanting Hare Krishna mantra. From their heart. They cannot be untouchable. They are touchable. By touching them. One will get very white. We will come back to them with a question. Hare Krishna. Hare Krishna. Comment. Yes,…”

One long question from the floor on protection and suffering, answered at length with stories of the Pandavas and of two senior Vaisnavas Maharaj has served.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:51 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj. Hare Krishna. Maharaj, I wanted to know that when you say devotees are fully protected by Krishna, so can you explain more? Like we see Amrish Maharaj, so he was protected from the curse of Durva Samuni. But we also see pure devotees in this world, they…”

children.topic: Q1 · If protected, why do devotees suffer?
children.note:
Ambarisa Maharaja was protected from Durvasa's curse, yet pure devotees — Jayapataka Swami, Maharaj's own guru with cancer — appear to suffer terribly to a neophyte's eye. How should we understand it, and are neophyte devotees also fully protected?

🎙 Maharaj at 40:54 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, I wanted to know that when you say devotees are fully protected by Krishna, so can you explain more? Like we see Amrish Maharaj, so he was protected from the curse of Durva Samuni. But we also see pure devotees in this world, they are suffering so much like uh his at…”

Maharaj's answer is categorical and he repeats it through the rest of the class: a pure devotee never suffers, and one who suffers is not a pure devotee. — “A pure devotee never suffers.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:49 (auto-transcript): “A pure devotee never suffers. A pure devotee never suffers. One who suffers is not a pure devotee. When we look at the life of the Pandavas, what do we see?”

Fatherless, raised among enemies who watched them as a snake watches a frog, nearly burnt alive, poisoned, driven out, their wife dragged into the assembly, at war all their lives — did they ask Krishna why? No. Their mother Kunti prayed for more calamity, because more anxiety meant coming closer to Krishna. — “Every day, you wake up to see people who don't like you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:10 (auto-transcript): “When we look at the life of the Pandavas, what do we see? Innumerable anxiety. Pandavas. They didn't see their father.”

children.topic: Hanuman: you made the Lord your messenger
children.note:
Maharaj retells Hanuman glorifying the Pandavas: the Supreme Lord is under their control, serving as their messenger. He plays out the exchange — who do you worship, who is greater, brahmachari or householder, where does Krishna stay? — to show that the Lord used the Pandavas to teach us the extent of their tolerance. Are we tolerant? No; the difference is bhakti.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:42 (auto-transcript): “so Hanumanji I told Narayanji the people who have gotten the mercy of Krishna are the Pandavas oh Pandavas you are great you have a magical You are supposed to control the Supreme Lord. You made Krishna. You are servant, your messenger.”

Maharaj's spiritual master, his body broken by cancer, asked Radhanath Swami to read Caitanya-caritamrta and shouted, we are there! — participating, not just hearing. In his book Surrender he defines transcendence: if difficulty changes your consciousness you are not transcendental; if it only increases your attachment to guru and Krishna, you are. He wrote it because he lived it, and Vaisnavas' writing, done only to glorify Krishna, needs no editing.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:12 (auto-transcript): “My special master, which you quoted, requested his holiness Radhanam Maharaj. Read. Yeah. He was hearing and he shouted, We are there! We are there! We are there! We are there! We are there! Where? Where? Where? Where? Where? Where? He was participating. He was participating.…”

Jayapataka Swami, in a sick body in which even a healthy man would find travel hard, travels to spread Krishna consciousness. In Mayapur last year Maharaj watched him, unable to stand, lifted onto the stage to perform abhiseka with a long-handled conch — determination, not suffering; a suffering man sits in his room waiting for death. By contrast, before Bhakti Tirtha Swami left, dying, he agreed to give class in a US temple while a healthy godbrother declined because he was tired. Which of the two is suffering?

🎙 Maharaj at 58:12 (auto-transcript): “Coming to Vishalini Jabhataka Swamaj. Is he complaining? Is he complaining? Krishna why you put me in such a situation? What is this? He never felt like that. Because it is very difficult for a healthy person. For a healthy person.”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 10 · I Worship the Son of Nanda Maharaja

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · I Worship the Son of Nanda Maharaja
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.77–96 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Vallabha Bhattacharya takes Mahaprabhu across the Yamuna, where the sight of the black water throws the Lord into ecstasy, then hosts him with full worship and prasada at Adaila. Raghupati Upadhyaya arrives and recites his verse: let others worship the Vedas, Smriti or Mahabharata — I worship Nanda, in whose courtyard the Supreme plays. Maharaj draws out why Krishna, not Ramacandra, can carry his father's shoes on his head: in Vrindavan Godhood is covered and only prema rules. Q&A on Rama versus Krishna, whether one's nature can really change, whose feet to worship, and crowd-pulling speakers. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Vallabha Bhattacharya takes Mahaprabhu and his associates by boat to his home for lunch. On seeing the glossy black water of the Yamuna the Lord cries out and leaps in; the boat tilts and fills, everyone is terrified, and though the Lord tries to restrain himself before Vallabha his ecstatic love cannot be checked.

Maharaj asks what the stimulant constantly working on Mahaprabhu is. It is the Yamuna — her blackish water reminds him of Krishna, and once the stimulant is in front of him the love flows by itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:23 (auto-transcript): “What is the stimulant? It'són's water. Jhamuna. Jhamuna. Jhamuna made his avant-garde to use his avant-garde. Black. Stimulant. Both them are cooking and may boil. So, it will boil.”

Put a pot of water on a burning flame and it will boil whatever you intend; you cannot ask it not to. Maharaj uses this to explain why, once the stimulant is present, pure love must show itself even when the Lord tries to pray and hold it in.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:59 (auto-transcript): “Both them are cooking and may boil. So, it will boil. So, So if there is something that is being done, then it will be done. So both of them, in the evening and evening, both of them, gave them the wisdom of Krishna's wisdom. That is pure love. That is the pure love of…”

children.topic: Could not hide it from Vallabha
children.note:
Mahaprabhu did not want to display his ecstasy before Vallabha Bhattacharya, who did not yet know him intimately, yet he could not control it. Maharaj asks: in such a case, what should he do? It simply flows.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:23 (auto-transcript): “He didn't want to show it before Balabacharya. But he couldn't control. In this case, what should he do? It is flowing. The problem is that the devotees are not in sight. !”
The Lord becomes calm, the boat reaches Adaila, and Vallabha Bhattacharya, fearing for the Lord's welfare, keeps him close and brings him home, where he receives him with full honour.

children.topic: Feet washed, water on every head
children.note:
Vallabha offers the Lord a fine seat and personally washes his feet; then he and his whole family sprinkle that water over their heads. The reading is done in English and Hindi.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:46 (auto-transcript): “When Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Valla Bhattacharya, being greatly pleased, offered the Lord his nice sitting place and personally washed his feet. I will not be able to die in my life, and I will not be able to die in my life.”

children.topic: Worship with incense, flowers and lamps
children.note: New cloth is offered and the Lord is worshipped with scented aguru, flowers and lamps. Maharaj lets the reading carry the picture of a householder receiving the Lord as a guest.

Vallabha has Balabhadra Bhattacharya cook, serves the Lord with great care and affection, and feeds Rupa Gosvami and his brother Vallabha (Anupama) too; the remnants go to Rupa Gosvami and Krishnadasa.

children.topic: Rupa and his brother also fed
children.note:
The two brothers, Rupa Gosvami and Sri Vallabha, are offered food along with the Lord, and Vallabha Bhattacharya then feeds Rupa Gosvami and Krishnadasa on the Lord's remnants.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:46 (auto-transcript): “Rupa Goswami and Sri Vallabh both brothers and sisters were also offered the food. The Siddhartha Mahaprabhu was offered lunch with great fear and affection. The brothers Rupa Goswami and Sri Vallabh were also offered the food. Vada achara Sri Rupa Doya ilaha wa sasa Vala…”

After lunch the Lord is given spices to freshen his mouth and made to rest while Vallabha massages his legs; only when the Lord sends him does the host go to take prasada himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:07 (auto-transcript): “The Lord was then given spices to purify his mouth. Afterwards, he was made to rest. And Vallabha Bhattacharya personally massaged his legs. While Vala Bhattacharya was assurging him, the Lord asked him to go take Prasada.”
Raghupati Upadhyaya of Tirhut, a learned scholar, great devotee and respected gentleman, comes to see the Lord, offers obeisances and receives a blessing.

From the purport Maharaj notes that Tirhut or Tirhutiya is the combined area of Saran, Champaran, Muzaffarpur and Darbhanga in Bihar; its people are called Tirhutiya.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:17 (auto-transcript): “Papa said Tiruhita or Tiruhutia is a combination of four districts in Bihar, Saran, Champaran, Uzafadbu, and Darabanga. The people of this state are called Thirupatiya. Ansi te nho kaila prabhu racharana bandana, Krishna mati rahupali prabhu racharana. Raghupati upadhyayanae…”

Raghupati first offers his respects and the Lord blesses him: remain always in Krishna consciousness. He is delighted to hear it, and the Lord then asks him to describe Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:01 (auto-transcript): “and Mahaprabhu has said to him that he is a Sadaiva Krishna Bhavna Bhavit Bane Raho Bhagupati Upadhyaya first offered his respect to Siddhita Mahaprabhu and the Lord gave him his blessing saying always stay in Krishna consciousness Suni Anandita He used to hear the Lord's…”

children.topic: 19.93–96 — Let others worship; I worship Nanda
children.note: Asked to describe Krishna, Raghupati recites verses of his own composition and the Lord is overwhelmed. The verse later placed in Rupa Gosvami's Padyavali: others may worship Sruti, Smriti or Mahabharata out of fear of material existence — he worships Nanda, in whose courtyard the Absolute Truth plays.

children.topic: Worship out of fear is elementary
children.note:
Maharaj says worship driven by fear of suffering is elementary; those who study the scriptures to be free from sin are serving their own interest, not worshipping God. That is not pure devotion in the full sense.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:14 (auto-transcript): “Those who are afraid of material existence. They worship Vedic Literatures, that is worship of fear, of suffering, it's elementary, it's elementary, Worshiping or a lot of fear or suffering is not pure devotion in the sense.”

children.topic: Nanda's power: Krishna as his son
children.note:
Why worship Nanda Maharaja? Because he has a power no one else has — the power of pure love that keeps the Supreme as his small child, playing in his house.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:19 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj Nanda Maharaj Nanda has a power what is his power his power is pure of God to keep Krishna as his song Krishna is playing in his house in his house in a small child and Nanda Maharaj He says, Krishna, go and bring my foot away. Krishna will go and bring me my foot away.”

Maharaj paints the scene: Nanda says, Krishna, bring my footwear, and the little boy comes carrying his father's shoes, very happy. Raghupati is watching and asking us — is this God? Is this the activity of God? — “Is this the activity of God?”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:53 (auto-transcript): “He says, Krishna, go and bring my foot away. Krishna will go and bring me my foot away. Krishna will go and bring me my foot away. He is very happy. With a big house. You see, I'm carrying my father's shoe and my hands. He is coming to give his father, and Agapati Padda is…”

Maharaj presses the room again and again: would Lord Ramacandra carry his father's shoes? Rama went to the forest on his father's order — that is fine, but this is different. He insists on a yes or no rather than a question in reply. — “Questions should be answered”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:59 (auto-transcript): “Would Ramachandra do like that? Ramachandra would do like that? Ramachandra would do like that? Ramachandra. He would do like this? Yes, say something”

Maharaj asks whether Vishnu would do this, and what is missing in Vishnu — father, mother, brothers, sisters? Then he turns to Rama to show what is missing even there: the full sweetness of relationships that only Vrindavan has.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:07 (auto-transcript): “Vishnu will do this? So Vishnu is missing something, isn't it? Vishnu is missing? What is that? Father? Mother? Sisters? Brother? He says spiritual mathematics have to answer the question.”

children.topic: Rama has friends, but with reverence
children.note:
Rama has father, mother and brothers, but no sister, and his friendship is friendship with reverence. Sugriva is a friend — but would he climb on Rama's shoulders or tease him, what kind of big man are you? He cannot. So something is missing.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:14 (auto-transcript): “What is their father, mother, brother, sister is missing, sister is missing, who is his sister? Machana's sister has four brothers, what is sister? her sister daughter one daughter how did you get this daughter from”

children.topic: Godhead prominent in Rama, sonhood in Krishna
children.note:
In Ramacandra the position of Godhead is prominent in his personality. In Krishna in Vrindavan the mood of Godhead is absent and the mood of a son is one hundred percent present.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:38 (auto-transcript): “so in Lanma Chandra the position of God is present is he not the position of God is is full is full he is Bhagawan prominent in his personality Godhead is prominent in Krishna”

Krishna in Vrindavan is dominated by prema, not by his Godhood; friendship there is complete, with friends of equal strength, which Rama, who is one, does not have. So Krishna, with all pride, puts his father's shoe on his head: I am the son of my father. — “only prema exists here”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:33 (auto-transcript): “the sonhood is present so Krishna is in Vrindavan dominated by Prem not by God the mood of God does not exist in Krishna the mood of a son is 100% present It's fully present.”

Four questions: Rama's sonhood versus Krishna's, whether one's nature can really change, whose feet we should worship, and why unqualified speakers draw crowds.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:33 (auto-transcript): “questions, comments yes so Raghupati Upadhyaya a pure devotee worship Krishna in Vrindavan by offering obeisances to”

children.topic: Q1 · Why would Rama not carry Dasaratha's shoes?
children.note:
A devotee restates the point — Raghupati worships Nanda, whose love gives Krishna full freedom to enjoy without the sentiment of Godhead — and asks whether some reverence in Rama obstructs his sonhood.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:59 (auto-transcript): “so Raghupati Upadhyaya a pure devotee worship Krishna in Vrindavan by offering obeisances to Maharashtra and they Nanda Maharaj who is doing and doing Pranam Arpit Whose love is giving Krishna full exercise to enjoy his sin, fully, full freedom to enjoy, without the sentiment…”

children.topic: Godhood full in Rama, so some things he cannot do
children.note:
Maharaj repeats: the Personality of Godhead is full in Ramacandra, therefore certain things he cannot do. In Krishna there is no Godhood on show; it is his sonhood that is prominent.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:03 (auto-transcript): “If I remember, I said personality of Godhead is food in Ramachandra therefore certain things”

children.topic: One wife, or 16,108 and the gopis
children.note:
Can Rama marry two wives? Never. Krishna married 16,108 legally and then, as Maharaj puts it, illegally called other men's wives into the forest at midnight. Rama would not do that even in a dream.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:06 (auto-transcript): “prominent here. Amachandha can marry two wives? Why not? Why are you gonna marry two? How many How much Krishna did Krishna do this? Legally, 16,000. 16,108. Illegally. Illegally.”

children.topic: The yajna-sitas and the groups of gopis
children.note:
When Sita was away Rama, as a kshatriya, needed a wife for sacrifice, so golden images of Sita were made; they came to life and asked to be his wives. Rama said: next life. Those yajna-sitas, with the personified Srutis and the sages, joined Krishna as gopis — three groups from this side, making four groups of gopis in all.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:14 (auto-transcript): “When Sita Devi left Externally So to say left externally As a shatriya You cannot do jagia without a wife So he will mold image of Sita And keep her inside Then completely jagia After everything was done After all these molded images became life.”

children.topic: Q2 · Does core nature ever change?
children.note:
Yesterday it was said a dog-eater becomes better than a brahmana by devotional service, yet devotees also say one's core nature or jati-samskara never changes. How to reconcile this?

🎙 Maharaj at 45:47 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, so my question is from yesterday's class. It's been said that dog eater becomes best of Brahmana by doing devotional service to God Krishna. but then we hear sometimes that no matter what the core nature or the jati samskar never changes so how to understand…”

children.topic: If nothing changes, what is bhakti for?
children.note:
Maharaj answers with a question: if I cannot become a pure devotee, why am I doing this? We practise because we can change, we are changing, and eventually we will change completely. Sanatana Gosvami's statement is that the pure devotee and the holy name can change anyone. — “we are doing this because we can change”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:32 (auto-transcript): “If he doesn't change, what do they use of bhakti? What do they use? if I cannot become pure devotee so why am I doing this we are doing this because we can change we are changing”

Krishna told Uddhava that whoever takes up his process will succeed, because it is a blazing fire. Wet wood takes longer — the water must dry first and the wood may bend — and some of us are like that; dry wood, light karma, burns fast. Either way it burns, provided it stays in the fire.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:25 (auto-transcript): “it's a blazing fire Anything You put in the fire To change If you put Wet wood In the fire It will take longer time To dry the water it will bend the wood some of us are like that we are like a wet wood”

children.topic: Api cet — even the most sinful
children.note: Maharaj opens Gita 4.36 and points to the word api cet, even if: even the worst of sinners crosses the ocean of misery by transcendental knowledge, and chapter 9 says the same for bhakti. Krishna is speaking — whom else should we believe? If the process can purify anyone from any level, the pious brahmana is no problem.

children.topic: We are here for a change
children.note:
Maharaj does not want to waste his time here unless change is possible, and he has seen the process do it. Prabhupada said: stick to this process and your success is guaranteed. Those without faith may go where they like; Maharaj stays with Prabhupada, because Prabhupada changed him. — “We are here for a change”

🎙 Maharaj at 56:52 (auto-transcript): “We are here for a change I don't want to waste my time to be here Because I want to change I have seen this process can do it Stick our head here And Prabhupada said stick to this process your success is guaranteed Krishna is speaking Krishna is speaking stick to this person…”

children.topic: Q3 · Whose feet should we worship?
children.note:
Moved by Vallabha washing the Lord's feet and worshipping him with incense and lamps, a devotee asks whether we should do this only for the spiritual master or for other saintly persons who come into our life.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:10 (auto-transcript): “Yes, I wanted to ask you a question. Hare Krishna. I found so beautiful how Shaitanya Mahaprabhu would jump in the water and go in the boat and started to maintain his external mood for Don't Disturb, what about Acharya? And then after his worship, he worshiped his lotus feet…”

The purport names two: our spiritual master and other saintly persons. Our guru is a sadhu, and when another pure devotee of that level comes to our house we should not refuse to wash his feet because he is not our guru. — “Guru will not protect you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:51 (auto-transcript): “It is mentioned, our spiritual master, and other saintly persons, two were mentioned, not only guru, two persons were mentioned, so it is not only a guru that is a sadhu, other devotees who are on that level, they are also sadhus. So your Guru is a Sadhu. So if your Guru is a…”

We have the right to worship our own guru, but if we offend other gurus we should not imagine our guru will shield us; by that behaviour we have become a disgrace to him.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:00 (auto-transcript): “So, we have right to worship our Guru. We shouldn't offend other Gurus. We shouldn't think that, if you do that, your Guru will protect you. Guru will not protect you. Because you are a disgrace to him. Makes sense? Thank you. Yes. Hare Krishna, thank you very much Maharaj.”

children.topic: Q4 · Why do unqualified speakers draw crowds?
children.note:
From the morning class: without empowerment one cannot preach — yet some who do not follow strictly are impactful speakers with large followings. How is Krishna empowering them?

🎙 Maharaj at 62:44 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, thank you very much Maharaj. Maharaj, my question is from today's morning class. Maharaj, like you mentioned, without empowerment, one cannot preach. and sometimes we see that people or sometimes devotees they don't follow much but still they are very impactful…”

children.topic: Six seasons: by nature or by force
children.note:
When Krishna was present all six seasons appeared together, happily and by their own nature; under Hiranyakasipu the seasons were also present, but by force and out of fear. People congregate in many places; the question is what is drawing them.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:24 (auto-transcript): “When Krishna was here Physically. Six seasons were present. When Hiran Kashipu took over power.”

children.topic: The disciple's hotel and the guru's temple
children.note:
A powerful motivational speaker visited a town and held his programme in a big hotel because the temple could not hold his audience; his own guru came to the same place and the temple room was not full. Devotees phoned Maharaj in dismay. He laughed — do you know what is happening?

🎙 Maharaj at 65:29 (auto-transcript): “He is one of the, how do they call them, motivational speaker. Motivational speaker. One of the very powerful one. He visited one temple. He didn't give class in the temple. Because his audience. It's more than the temple. So he had his program in a bigger hotel.”

children.topic: Mahabharata thrills, Bhagavatam puts us to sleep
children.note:
Maharaj asks how we feel reading Mahabharata — excited, hair standing on end. And Bhagavatam? Sleep. People run after show-bottle devotees because we are low-class people attracted to stories; taste is the issue, and very few are attracted to the real thing.

🎙 Maharaj at 67:22 (auto-transcript): “When you read Mahabharat, how do you feel? When you are reading Mahabharat, how do you feel? How do you feel? Courage. How do you feel when you read Mahabharat? We are excited Yes, really excited When you read Bhagavatam, do you feel this way? But when you study Bhagavatam,…”

children.topic: Check what the crowd gives up
children.note:
Of the million who gather, how many become pure devotees, stop smoking, give up tea, onion and garlic, and take to pure chanting? Count that number, and then judge the empowerment. — “So we should check.”

🎙 Maharaj at 70:46 (auto-transcript): “So we should check. After the million people who have gathered there, how many of them are becoming pure devotees? How many of them have stopped smoking? How many of them are giving up tea, garlic and onion, how many of the million people here, how many have given up these…”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 11 · The Best of All in Krishna's Pastimes

nodeData.topic: Day 11 · The Best of All in Krishna's Pastimes
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.97–102 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Raghupati Upadhyaya tells Mahaprabhu that Krishna is the best of all beings, Syamasundara the best of his forms and Mathura the best of his abodes. Maharaj compares Dwarka, Mathura and Vrindavan — opulence, knowledge and pure love — and asks why the Brajavasis cry if Krishna never leaves Vrindavan. The answer unfolds through the sugarcane-juice analogy, the Prema Sarovara pastime, Uddhava's lessons from Mother Yashoda and the gopis, and Haridasa Thakura's beating. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Asked by the Lord to recite more, Raghupati Upadhyaya offers his respects and speaks a verse wondering to whom he can say that the Supreme Lord is wandering with the gopis on the banks of the Yamuna. Hearing it, Mahaprabhu is absorbed in ecstatic love.

children.topic: Minds slacken on the material side
children.note:
Maharaj notes from the purport that our minds and bodies are normally busy with material activities; when they are activated on the spiritual platform, they go slack on the material one — as the Lord's did on hearing of Krishna's pastimes.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:52 (auto-transcript): “and body slackened our minds and bodies are always engaged in material activities when they are activated on a spiritual platform they slacken on the material platform When Raghupati Upadhyayai saw Sita Mahaprabhu”

Seeing the Lord's ecstasy, Raghupati Upadhyaya concludes that he is Krishna himself. Mahaprabhu then quizzes him: who is the chief of all beings, and which of Krishna's millions of forms is best? He answers Krishna, and the flute-playing Syamasundara form.

To the question which of Krishna's abodes is best, Raghupati Upadhyaya answers Madhupuri, Mathura-dhama. Maharaj reminds the room that this is Mahaprabhu training the brothers' understanding before the formal teaching to Rupa Gosvami.

Maharaj asks the room how many places Krishna lived in — Vrindavan, Mathura and Dwarka — and grades them. Each is complete, yet one is more complete than another; he calls this spiritual relativity, as distinct from material relativity.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:48 (auto-transcript): “So, Lord Krishna lived in three places. How many places? So, Bhagavan lived in three places or in three places? Vrindavan, Mathura, Dwarka. Vrindavan, Mathura and Dwarka. So, Dwarka is a place of opulence. Dwarka is aishwarya maya. So, it is complete.”

Dwarka is aisvarya-maya — palaces, parijata trees, queens, horses and elephants. It is complete, but the mood is one of majesty.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:18 (auto-transcript): “So, Dwarka is a place of opulence. Dwarka is aishwarya maya. So, it is complete. This is Poon, Ashwadi, Parades of Palaces, Parijat, Parijat, a lot of queens, queens, horses, elephants,”

In Mathura the knowledge that Krishna is the Personality of Godhead is present, so it is more complete than Dwarka. That is why Devaki and Vasudeva offer prayers to their newborn son — they know who he is. — “This is spiritual relativity, spiritual relativity.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:38 (auto-transcript): “In Mathura? Knowledge. The personality of God is there. So, more complete. This is spiritual relativity, spiritual relativity. we have material relativity we have also spiritual relativity so in Mathura”
