With good sadhana everything unfolds gradually, with no need to jump. A student sitting the class 1 exam does not need to ask who teaches class 2; reach there and the teacher is there. — “The first consideration for all of our devotees is good sadhana.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:00 (auto-transcript): “The first consideration for all of our devotees is good sadhana. If we have good sadhana, everything will simultaneously, gradually unfold. You don't have to jump. Just like if a student has an exam in class 1. You don't need to ask who is the teacher in class 2.”

Who writes is not a political appointment; it comes naturally, and not everyone writes. Jiva Gosvami trained devotees on Rupa Gosvami's books and the Gosvamis edited one another's work as a team — that too fulfils the principle. Follow our standard and there is no need to debate it.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:26 (auto-transcript): “To write books, it should not be, no, you should write, you should not write yet, it's not by appointment, it's not a political thing, everything will come naturally. And, it is not everybody who write, although the assignment is given to all, some were not”

children.topic: Q2 · Chanting when pure devotees are absent
children.note:
In the morning class Maharaj had said chanting in the company of pure devotees gives the name its meaning. When they are not physically present, should we imagine them, and how?

🎙 Maharaj at 43:05 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Krishna Gurudev, thank you for the lecture. In the morning class, you were mentioning that chanting with pure devotees, the name gives a meaning. So just now you told that we should imagine Rupa and Sanatangaswami dancing in the mind's eye. So when the pure devotees are…”

The answer is in the verse: Rupa and Sanatana remembered Mahaprabhu's pastimes — they meditated on him and so were with him. We should likewise remember and pray to the acaryas and see them with us; if we forget them they are absent, if we remember them they are always there. — “Always see them present with us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:15 (auto-transcript): “It is mentioned here. There is a change in Rupa Sanatana Goswami. They do what? They remember Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's past times. What is that? They are meditating on that. So, what are they? They were together with Chaitanya Mahap. That is what we should do.”

children.topic: Q3 · Why reveal madhurya-rasa in Kali-yuga?
children.note:
Vyasadeva did not reveal the rasas in earlier ages. Why would the Lord reveal the highest, madhurya-rasa, in an age where people are unfortunate, dull and unable to manage even the basics of bhakti?

🎙 Maharaj at 45:53 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Shila Gurudev, thank you for the class. Shila Gurudev, the rasas, as you mentioned, they are in the higher mood. And Shila Vedhyas Ji, he did not reveal the rasas in the previous Yuga. So in Kali Yuga, the people generally are very unfortunate and they are very…”

children.topic: A fortunate age because Mahaprabhu came
children.note:
That is our fortune. This Kali-yuga holds something not found in Satya-yuga or the other ages, because Caitanya Mahaprabhu appeared in it — and he does not come in every Kali-yuga. He brought this treasure, so we should take advantage of it.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:58 (auto-transcript): “That is our fortune. They say that this Kali Yuga is a fortunate age. It's not there in Satya. It was not in Sakti Yuga. Later. Later. Later. Later. Later. Later. Later. Later. Later. Later. It's about fortune. It's about fortune. That we have something which is not there in…”

children.topic: Krishna book before the earlier cantos
children.note:
In the same spirit Prabhupada published the Krishna book — the Tenth Canto — before the earlier cantos of the Bhagavatam and distributed it to non-devotees. Not a mistake but deliberate, so that it would deliver them.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:31 (auto-transcript): “Shilapwapad published Christian book before, before. Shilapwapad published Christian book which is 10th canto before, before, before 4.5. In the book of Krishna, the book of Bhagavatam, he wrote it in the book of Krishna, and he wrote it in the book of Krishna, and he wrote…”

children.topic: Q4 · Wanting to sacrifice, but body and mind refuse
children.note:
A mataji asks: we are inspired to sacrifice everything for Krishna, but our body, mind and present stage do not allow it. Do we need some adhikara even to sacrifice as much as we wish, and how do we progress?

🎙 Maharaj at 50:23 (auto-transcript): “that we should also sacrifice everything for Krishna. But Guruji, when we get inspired and when we try to sacrifice, so our body and mind and our current stage doesn't allow, we face a lot of problems. So Guruji, what I have said is that even to sacrifice and move there to…”

children.topic: Beg and cry for the strength
children.note:
The acaryas did not come to make a show but to teach us what is possible. Since the mind troubles us, we beg: My Lord, nirjala is difficult for me, you introduced it for my benefit but my karma is heavy, please help me. When they see our sincerity they bless us with strength. — “you should practice begging and crying for the mercy of the Lord”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:11 (auto-transcript): “These acharyas, they didn't come here to make a show. They came here to teach us what is possible. So our minds are troubling. Therefore, we should beg. She will cry. With her mercy. When they see our sincerity.”

Why is one of the twenty-four Ekadasis called Pandava Nirjala? Bhima, who had never fasted in his life, pleaded that a fire burned in his stomach and was pacified only by eating. Told he must fast at least once, he resolved, cried, and fasted, his whole body shaking. Hence the blessing: fast on this day and you are credited with the remaining Ekadasis.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:16 (auto-transcript): “You know why one of the 24 Ekarajis became so special? Which one? Pandava Nirjali Ekarajis. Because this is the only one, only once, being fasted in his entire life. And Vyasi Dev was narrating in the past times, and he said, all of you must,”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 16 · Krishna is Interested in Love

nodeData.topic: Day 16 · Krishna is Interested in Love
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.133–135 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Rupa Gosvami calls himself the lowest of men yet writes because the Lord inspired him from within — Maharaj shows this is the humility of all acaryas, who do nothing on their own. Stories of Isvara Puri, Vallabha Bhatta and the banana peels teach that Krishna looks for love and selfless service, not expertise or position, and that a sincere, eager servant is empowered whatever his external situation. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 19.133 — Rupa Gosvami on the Lord's mercy
children.note: The verse introduces Rupa Gosvami's own words about Mahaprabhu's mercy, spoken in the invocation of his Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu. Maharaj continues the chapter from text 133 with the Hindi translation read alongside.

children.topic: 19.134 — Lowest of men, yet inspired to write
children.note: Rupa Gosvami's invocation verse: he has no qualification, yet the inspiration to write about devotional service was given to him, so he bows to the Lord who gave him the chance.

children.topic: Who dares speak to such an audience?
children.note:
Maharaj recalls Rupa Gosvami asking who his readers are — exalted Vaishnavas with the power to chastise demigods. How dare he speak on this subject? Because the Lord instructed him to write. Maharaj gives his analogy: if a sudra lights the fire, does the food still cook? Yes — the potency is in the order, not in the person. That is pure humility.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:28 (auto-transcript): “Who are my audience? The exalted Vaisna Vais who have power to chastise demigods. How dare you speak about this subject matter? I have the power to do that because I was instructed by the Shiva to write the book.”

One may have no qualification to speak on transcendental topics, yet be given the power. Maharaj recalls a devotee told by Mahaprabhu to speak the glories of the holy name: he protested that he knew nothing, and the Lord replied that the scriptures live in his heart, so speak. Acaryas do nothing on their own; they are authorised, and they bring out what is placed in them. — “they don't do anything on their own”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:42 (auto-transcript): “It's a qualification to speak about trans-letter topics. that one does not have the qualification to do it but he has been or she has many power to do I want I want to hear the glories of the holy name from you. My Lord, you are asking a question on each person.”

The author of this very book had the same experience. Old, hands trembling as he wrote, he calls himself lame and foolish — yet he writes, because he was directed to. Maharaj stresses the trembling was not from disease but from devotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:51 (auto-transcript): “krishnada has covered kushwami who wrote this the same experience i am lame and ill-advised old my hands shaking he's writing it was already old he's so he's writing is trembling he's not trembling from all ages pakistan you know it's pakistan pakistan he's not he's not…”

Maharaj cites Mahaprabhu's own statement that what the acaryas write does not need correcting, because they write as instruments of the Lord. Yet the Lord's spiritual master still asked him to read his book and find faults.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:22 (auto-transcript): “So Chita Mahaprabhu said himself whatever our acharyas have written does not need correction. they are writing at a pillar for Godhead therefore there can never be an error or mistakes inside still his Purusha Master”

children.topic: Too humble to serve is arrogance
children.note:
The Lord agreed the book was correct, but his guru insisted he read it anyway — this is service. Maharaj's lesson: a devotee should never be so humble that he refuses service; that is not humility but pride. — “a devotee should not be too humble”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:35 (auto-transcript): “a devotee should not be too humble to refuse service that is not humility it is arrogance so once the time abu was uttered by his guru go through it see some fault and tell me sitamu took the book went to eat and he came back this word it should not be”

Ordered by his guru to find a fault, Nimai Pandit took the book, returned and pointed to one word. Isvara Puri checked all night, came back the next day and showed the word was correct, and the Lord agreed. Maharaj quotes Vrindavana dasa Thakura: the Lord accepted defeat from his devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:48 (auto-transcript): “so once the time abu was uttered by his guru go through it see some fault and tell me sitamu took the book went to eat and he came back this word it should not be it should not be Atma Nipoti.”

This is the platform on which the acaryas operate: pure instruments of the Lord, no selfish motive. We do not write to show scholarship; it is pure devotional service, prompted by Krishna in a compassionate heart. — “we don't write books to show our scholarship”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:46 (auto-transcript): “where our acharyas operate pure of our godhead no selfish motivations inside we don't write books to show our scholarship it is pure devotional service because it is motivated by Krishna to their heart who has compassion the Lord will”

By contrast Maharaj tells of a learned acarya whom Mahaprabhu turned away. He asks the room how many times he came, and walks through both visits to show what pride and scholarship without humility lead to.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:35 (auto-transcript): “so Chetan Mahaprabhu rejected who is that? he came to Chetan Mahaprabhu he came to Chetan Mahaprabhu and he said written commentary. Powerful. But I did not touch one word from Siddharth Swami. Siddharth Swami said, poor astute.”

He came boasting a powerful commentary that did not depend on Sridhara Svami. Mahaprabhu would not hear it: whoever does not follow Sridhara Svami is useless. I know nothing, I just chant Hare Krishna — what you have written is for you, not for me. Go.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:58 (auto-transcript): “written commentary. Powerful. But I did not touch one word from Siddharth Swami. Siddharth Swami said, poor astute. Cannot hear it. Go away. Anyone who does not follow Siddharth Swami is useless. Siddharth Swami is speaking. For me, I don't know anything as I'm chanting Hare…”

children.topic: Why call your husband by name?
children.note:
The second time he went to Advaita Acarya with a clever question: scripture says a chaste wife does not call her husband by name; we are all prakriti, wives of Krishna — so why do you call Krishna, Krishna, Krishna?

🎙 Maharaj at 19:54 (auto-transcript): “Second time, he came to Advaita Acharya. In the scripture A chaste wife Doesn't call the husband by name We are all prakriti So We are wives to Krishna Why are you calling your husband by name Krishna, Krishna, Krishna why you are not just you are not just”

children.topic: Advaita sends him to the Lord
children.note:
Advaita Acarya said the Lord is here, ask him. Maharaj calls this the intelligence of a disciple — he knew the answer and knew the man was foolish, but would not chastise him himself. When devotees stop attending to us and leave us to Krishna, we are in a very dangerous position. — “means we're in a very dangerous position”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:44 (auto-transcript): “he said my dear the Lord is here you can ask me a question ask the Lord a question that's intelligence of an intelligent disciple he didn't answer he sent him to the Lord so the Lord would just ask him Advetta knows the answer he knows he's foolish”

Is he an acarya who knows scripture or a fool? He quotes scripture yet forgot it. Mahaprabhu answered with Gita 9.14: Krishna says chant my name always, and a bona fide disciple follows the order — so what is our fault? He could not answer and was sent away. It is painful; we should not be rejected like that.

How do we develop humility and lose pride? Good sadhana. Maharaj asks the best time for it — brahma-muhurta, which he calls Krishna's invitation. That hour supports our practice because focus and concentration are naturally there; we should take advantage of it to perfect our lives.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:06 (auto-transcript): “Humility. No pride. How do we develop that? Good sadhana. What is the best time for our sadhana? Brahmurta does what? Krishna's invitation. Brahmurta is Krishna's invitation.”
Mahaprabhu stays ten days at Prayag instructing Rupa Gosvami and investing him with the potency to do his work. Read with Hindi translation and the English purport.

Do we see this quality in Rupa Gosvami, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Srila Prabhupada and all acaryas? Yes — because they know that whatever they have done came from the Lord's inspiration in their hearts.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:40 (auto-transcript): “Do we see that quality in Rupa Goswami? Do we see that? Krishna does cover it in Goswami. Krishna Prabhupada and all of Acharyas they have these feelings why? they know that whatever they have done is due to the inspiration given by the Supreme Lord in their hearts this is…”

Who receives the understanding to come to Krishna? Those constantly — not sometimes — engaged in serving him with love, priti. Maharaj dwells on the word: it is the affection that draws Krishna's gift.

children.topic: Does Krishna give knowledge to jnanis?
children.note:
Maharaj asks the room. Yes — otherwise how would they speculate, and enjoy and be proud of it? The difference is that jnanis have no priti; they are selfish, so Krishna gives them ordinary knowledge but never reveals himself. Devotees can reach Krishna without knowledge; jnanis with knowledge do not. — “Krishna not only gives knowledge, Krishna gives himself to his devotees.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:27 (auto-transcript): “Krishna does not give knowledge to the jnanis? No? Yes, Krishna gives knowledge to jnanis? Yes, he gives them knowledge. Otherwise, how would they speculate? When they're speculating, it's very sweet. They enjoy it, they enjoy it, very proud of it because they are enjoying it…”

From the next purport: one may have a bona fide guru and institution and still lack the intelligence to grasp the teaching, yet if sincerely engaged in service Krishna himself enlightens him from within until he reaches him. He does this for a bhakta, never for a jnani.

Recalling the verse that only Krishna's devotee is desireless and peaceful, Maharaj lists those after enjoyment, liberation and mystic power: all self-centred, and so miserable. The devotee is calm, free and selfless. A non-devotee is dangerous, because what he does destroys himself and others — so become a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:48 (auto-transcript): “the jnanis are selfish devotees are selfless Krishna Bhakta, Nisga Mataiba, Santa, Bukti, Bukti, Siddhi, Asakali, no, no, Asakali, Asanta. The, the Buktis, Buktis, who are engaged in sanctification, Buktis, Buktis, the Buktis, who are engaged in liberation in cities”

The purport says a devotee's material position does not matter. Maharaj puts it simply: Krishna does not care for our expertise, only for our love — and proves it with the banana peels. — “Krishna is not interested in our expertise.”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:50 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Krishna is not interested in our expertise. He is interested in our love. Is he not? Krishna prefer banana peel is so opulent, opulent. Is it Boga or Prasada? Is it Boga or Prasada? I might see you answer my question. Jirodan invited Krishna please.”

Duryodhana, a prince whose cooks were brahmanas — unlike some of our temples with paid cooks, Maharaj remarks — invited Krishna to an irresistible feast, even with sukta. Krishna did not go. He went where banana peels were offered to him while the fruit itself was set aside.

Maharaj asks: a friend peels a fragrant banana, puts the fruit aside and hands you the peel — what do you do? Everyone would grab the banana. Krishna saw it right there, did not take it, and ate the peels until he was constipated. The beauty was not in the banana but in the love in the peels. — “the beauty is not in the banana, it is in the peels”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:27 (auto-transcript): “How do you do? What will you do? Visit a friend. He peel that banana very nicely. Aromatic and tasty banana. He put the banana away. And give you the peels. What will you do? What will you do? I will pick the banana because the banana is right there, it's right there, it's…”

The purport recalls that Rupa Gosvami was a government officer and householder working among mlecchas and yavanas, yet eager to serve and therefore fit for the Lord's mercy. Maharaj draws out what this means for how we see devotees around us.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:17 (auto-transcript): “Right. In his earlier life, Sir Rupa Goswami was a government officer and a greyhoster. He was not even a bhammachari or sanyasi, I can see. He associated with militias and yavanas. But because he was always eager to serve, he was a qualified recipient of the Lord's mercy. A…”

Liberated while living — here in this world, not elsewhere. When mind, body and intelligence are absorbed in Krishna, that is jivan-mukta, and there may be such souls among us. So we should not look at one another on the bodily platform but ask what the real position of the devotees around us is.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:17 (auto-transcript): “here in this material right here in the material is what jivanmukta right here not there here What is that? Our mind, our body, our intelligence is what?”

The acts of pure devotees confuse non-devotees; without purity one cannot understand purity. The brahmana community rejected Rupa Gosvami for working with mlecchas — externally. Internally he is Rupa Manjari, not sometimes but always; that position cannot change. — “One cannot understand a pure devotee”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:50 (auto-transcript): “Because activities where pure devotees are bewildering to non-devotees. One cannot understand a pure devotee except you are a pure devotee. Is he not? He is not. the purity you can't understand. Rupa Goswami was rejected by the Brahmana community.”

children.topic: Coming down to preach is no degradation
children.note:
When a pure devotee comes to the madhyama level to preach, is that a fall? No — like a professor holding a child's hand to teach writing. Both hands move the same way, but one is teaching and one is learning.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:16 (auto-transcript): “a pure devotee for him who had to preach come to Madhyam is that degradation? is that degradation? no it is not a degradation just like if a professor holds the hand of a child to teach the child how to write so is he learning or teaching? You see Lenny was teaching, but both…”

A man hired a tutor who guided his son's hand across the page. Afterwards the boy asked his father why he paid the man — I am writing ABCD myself. The father: you are a fool, that is why I brought a wise man. Maharaj: if he lets go of your hand, what can you write? He holds our hand out of compassion; it is not the same level. — “no he's holding our hand because of his compassion”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:01 (auto-transcript): “Chita Bautista Swati Takura told a story. That one man employed a teacher to teach his child. So the teacher carried the hand of the child was teaching him how to write. After teaching, when the teacher left, the son went to his father. Daddy? Daddy? Why did you pay this…”

Pure devotees move among us and do what we do in order to teach us, so we must not misjudge them. Equally, we must not be deceived into thinking that everyone who cheats us is a pure devotee holding our hand.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:06 (auto-transcript): “so we should be careful not to misunderstand We should be careful not to be deceived, to think that everybody who is cheating me is a pure devotee who is using my hand to teach my hand to write. We should be careful with that also, cheating. to teach oneself no to keep…”

One question from the floor about editing the acaryas' books, answered at length.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:39 (auto-transcript): “Comment? It could be your question. Sometimes apparently we see some faults in the writings, such as grammatical or consideration, shall be corrected because, in the words of corrective, Sometimes the message is a little bit changed or diverted. So what should the desire for…”

children.topic: Q1 · Should apparent faults in the books be corrected?
children.note:
Sometimes we see grammatical or punctuation faults in the writings, and sometimes a correction slightly changes or diverts the message. Should we leave it as it is, or correct it according to our understanding?

🎙 Maharaj at 50:53 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes apparently we see some faults in the writings, such as grammatical or consideration, shall be corrected because, in the words of corrective, Sometimes the message is a little bit changed or diverted. So what should the desire for us to leave it as it is or try to…”

Maharaj recalls the school exercise of paraphrasing: a full page reduced to five sentences that must carry the whole message. The examiner has read the page carefully and judges how well you understood it. Comparing your version with the original shows the weight of your understanding.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:38 (auto-transcript): “In English, we have that exercise. So you give it, you give it a full page. Paraphras. That's the word. Paraphras. Paraphras means a full page. You can make only five sentences.”

children.topic: Punctuation that keeps the message is bona fide
children.note:
A correction of punctuation must not change the original message; if it only makes the meaning clearer, it is bona fide.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:59 (auto-transcript): “So, punctuation should not change the original message. It will make it better for understanding. Therefore, it is bonafide. In the spiritual circle, we need the empowerment.”

children.topic: Beg for mercy, not academic ability alone
children.note:
In the spiritual circle we need empowerment to do such work nicely and perfectly, so we beg for the mercy rather than rely on academic skill. — “We need the empowerment.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:28 (auto-transcript): “In the spiritual circle, we need the empowerment. We need the empowerment. to be able to do it nicely, perfectly. So we beg for the mercy. Not only our academic ability. Beg for the mercy.”

From Maharaj's own experience: expert instrumentalists who make famous names playing for others cannot make music of their own. Left to themselves they keep changing the drum, the percussion, endlessly, and nothing is finished. Ordinary ability falls short of the glory of spirituality; beg for mercy very seriously and the service will succeed. — “So beg for mercy”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:13 (auto-transcript): “I have some experience. They are musicians, experts in playing instruments. They would never make music on their own. They can play for others. They make names, very famous. Those who play those instruments themselves, they cannot make the music.”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 17 · Queries So Far

nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19 — questions so far · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. No new verses today. Maharaj opens by remembering Sanatana Goswami — the four instructions, Shiva and the mosquitoes at Manasi Ganga, Radharani confirming Rupa's writing, the hidden sadhu at Pavan Sarovar — and shares a prayer to the spiritual master. Then four questions from the floor: is there a contradiction between wealth and renunciation, who were the buried Goswami books written for, where Pandu fits among Vyasadeva's sons, and how Rupa and Sanatana left this world. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj says today's reading is small, so he will share what comes to mind about the acaryas instead. Remembering them is very important: remembering them brings their blessings. — “Very important to remember our acharyas.”

🎙 Maharaj at 03:14 (auto-transcript): “So we have been trying to remember our acharyas. Very important to remember our acharyas. Remembering them will have their blessings. So Sanatana Goswami, who is here in this morning, was given an assignment.”

Maharaj asks the room how many assignments Mahaprabhu gave — five? six? ten? Four: discover the places of Krishna's pastimes, write books, deity worship, and preach Krishna consciousness. And they did it.

🎙 Maharaj at 03:47 (auto-transcript): “So Sanatana Goswami, who is here in this morning, was given an assignment. How many? Five? Six? Ten? How many? How many? four instructions one is discover all the past time places”

Vrindavan is not only this Raman Reti; it comprises twelve forests — Govardhan, Yavat, Gokul and the rest are all Vrindavan. The Goswamis wandered through all of it, so they are found everywhere.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:45 (auto-transcript): “Vrindavan is not only this Ramadreti. Vrindavan comprises of 12 forests. This is just one. So the whole of this area to Giraj, to Yavata, to Gokul, to Arifuye, they are all Grindavan. Sanatan Goswami, Rupa Goswami, and any other Goswami, they are everywhere.”

Sanatana Goswami is staying near Manasi Ganga, close to Haridev, where Shiva also resides. Huge mosquitoes bite him — no net, no repellent, no electricity in those days — and he decides to shift elsewhere the next day.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:34 (auto-transcript): “One time Sanatana Goswami was standing very close to Manasi Ganga. One time Sanatana Goswami was standing very close to Manasi Ganga. Manasi Ganga is very close to who? Manasi Ganga is close to Haridev. Manasi Ganga is close to Haridev.”

Maharaj points out that worms lived in Sanatana Goswami's body and he never complained; but the mosquitoes made it impossible to write, so he resolved to leave.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:17 (auto-transcript): “Sanatana Goswami, worms were living in this body, he didn't complain. Worms, he didn't complain. But mosquitoes were biting. So good, he's biting. But very uncomfortable. So Sanatana Goswami decided tomorrow I will shift from this place. I will go to a different place. So…”

Shiva appears: Prabhuji, please don't go, your association sustains me. From today no more mosquitoes here — he makes a natural mosquito net. Maharaj says people report it holds to this day, and invites anyone to go and spend a night to confirm. He adds he himself cannot sleep under a net; it suffocates him.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:58 (auto-transcript): “So Shiva came there. Prabhu Ji, please, don't go. Stay here. Your association is sustaining me. I want to stay here, don't go away. So Sanatana Goswami said, I want to stay here.”

children.topic: A prayer to the spiritual master
children.note:
Sanatana Goswami is Gauranga's dear associate and a spiritual master, and a guru has a powerful role in a disciple's life. Maharaj shares a prayer to the guru, attributed to Surdas, which a godbrother gave him, and invites the room to repeat it after him.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:21 (auto-transcript): “He is a spiritual master. Adhyatmik Guru. Very dear to Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. So, a Guru has a powerful role to play in the life of a disciple. So, there is a very beautiful prayer here. I had this for me, soliness in a Dumna Maharaj. It's a Surudas prayer. He's offering…”

children.topic: Do you see devotees as beautiful?
children.note:
The guru gave the kanthi-mala no gold can buy, the tilak, and the beautiful form of the devotee. Maharaj stops to ask: do you see devotees as beautiful, or as enemies? The guru gave us beautiful devotees; to make them enemies is very bad.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:25 (auto-transcript): “Do you see devotees as beautiful? Do you see devotees as beautiful? Or an enemy? or you see Shatru. Who do we see? Who do you see? Beautiful devotee. Beautiful devotee. The Guru gave us beautiful devotee. He would make them enemy.”

children.topic: One hand holds mine, one holds the lamp
children.note:
The guru offers shelter: with one hand he holds the disciple's hand, with the other the lamp of knowledge, and so leads him across the dark ocean of the material world. He deserves the greatest respect because only he can rescue us in the blink of an eye.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:33 (auto-transcript): “In one of his hands, he holds my own hand. and with his other hand he is holding the lamp of knowledge which helps me to cross over the dark ocean of material world. My guru desires the greatest respect because only he”

Srila Prabhupada signed his letters 'your ever well-wisher'. Ever means eternity: the guru remains our well-wisher eternally — not sometimes, but always there.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:15 (auto-transcript): “Shilaprabhupad signed his letter. You are well-wished. Okay, thank you. Thank you. You are ever well-wishah. Ever well-wishah means what? Eternity. Eternity. We remain our well-wishah eternally. Let's see Guru.”

Three more episodes show the Goswamis' way: Rupa's writing confirmed by Radharani herself, Sanatana hidden in the jungle at Pavan Sarovar, and devotees who dance without any instrument. Maharaj asks: are we not fortunate to have such personalities with us?

🎙 Maharaj at 18:13 (auto-transcript): “So one time. Shilorupa Goswami. He composes as usual. a book. So he describes Srimati Radha Rani's hair. What? Snake. Snake. So Sanatana Goswami said, what? Radha Rani's hair is snake.”

Rupa Goswami writes that Srimati Radharani's hair is a snake. Sanatana Goswami questions it, and Radharani herself arranges for him to see that what Rupa wrote is perfectly correct. Maharaj adds that she likes only black — the Yamuna, her dress, her hair, her eyes, and our best friend Syamasundara. Rupa, the second body of Mahaprabhu, has the blessing that whatever he writes is perfect.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:13 (auto-transcript): “So one time. Shilorupa Goswami. He composes as usual. a book. So he describes Srimati Radha Rani's hair. What? Snake. Snake. So Sanatana Goswami said, what? Radha Rani's hair is snake.”

When Sanatana Goswami was sent to make Pavan Sarovar a tirtha it was thick jungle — mosquitoes, scorpions, snakes, wild animals, no house, no food — and the villagers did not know he was there. Krishna came to him: Babuji, why stay here where nobody sees you? How will you eat? At least stay outside. But Sanatana was not looking for food.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:11 (auto-transcript): “in Pavan Sarovar Natan Goswami was staying there to stick bush nobody lived there He was hiding there, who would see him there? Last time we went there, they were constructing a temple. When Sanatana Goswami was sent there to make that place a Tirta, it was a big jungle.”

If somebody gives something they take it; if nothing comes, it is fine. Even what they accept, they accept to bless the giver, not because they like it.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:00 (auto-transcript): “so they don't beg if somebody gives something they take they don't beg some people beg this is Goswami they don't beg something comes they will take nothing comes it's okay and even something that comes it is because they want to bless those people not because they like it…”

We dance only when the kirtan has a nice mridanga, karatalas and sweet singing, otherwise we complain and ask for a different player. The Goswamis do not depend on instruments; just seeing a mridanga or karatalas was enough to set their Krishna consciousness ablaze, and they would dance and fall on the ground. — “Instrument doesn't make them dance.”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:56 (auto-transcript): “Goswami does not dance for instrument. Instrument doesn't make them dance. instrument doesn't make them dance they don't depend on instrument to dance they dance naturally without instrument so Simbridanga alone it is sufficient for them just to see Simbridanga or see Kartal…”

Maharaj closes the talk: Mahaprabhu trained Rupa and Sanatana in what they had to do, and only then sent them to Vrindavan to do their duty. Training is necessary before engagement. — “Training before engagement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:16 (auto-transcript): “So Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is training them. In what they have to do. Training is necessary. Training before engagement. So Rupa Sanatana Goswami have been trained. And they were sent to Vrindavan. To do their duty. All right. Is it not? Questions, comments.”

children.topic: Q1 · Millionaires, cooking, money is death?
children.note:
A devotee hears a contradiction across the recent classes: attending mangala-arati makes you a millionaire, a pure devotee must know how to cook, yet money is death — and Sanatana Goswami offered plain bread balls to Madana-mohana. Maharaj answers by asking how the Goswamis got what they needed.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:02 (auto-transcript): “I have I don't know if it's a question or a comment regarding this morning session and yesterday this morning you mentioned that if we attend Mangalartic we will become millionaire and also today in the morning you mentioned that if you want to become a pure devotee you need…”

children.topic: How did the Goswamis get ingredients?
children.note:
In the material world, to cook you need ingredients, and for ingredients you need money, so you work. Did the Goswami who wanted to make a feast take a job or collect donations? He was a poor man, yet got everything he needed. Sanatana Goswami wanted to build a temple — did he go for donations? All the Goswamis follow the same pattern.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:20 (auto-transcript): “In a material world, if we want to cook, what do we do? We want to cook. By the ingredients. But what? If you don't have money, what do you do? You work. You work to get money to buy the things you need.”

When Mahaprabhu discovered Radha Kund it was so small that only one person could enter; he and Acyutananda bathed in it, and he assigned Raghunatha Dasa Goswami to expand it. Raghunatha thought for a moment that he needed money and rebuked himself — a sannyasi thinking of money! Yet a wealthy man about to donate to a temple was told by the Lord to give it instead to a devotee at Radha Kund named Raghunatha Dasa. He came looking for him, Raghunatha accepted, and the kund we see today was made.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:30 (auto-transcript): “Raghunath Das Goswami was assigned to excavate Radha Kunt. When Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu discovered the Kunt, it was this size. Small, just small, small, only one person can enter, so Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu entered into it, and they came out, then, who was there with Shri…”

Raghunatha's father did business to make money; Raghunatha's business is Krishna consciousness. So pure devotees are at once renounced and wealthy. Is that a contradiction? That is the world of devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:35 (auto-transcript): “Raghunath Das Goswami's business to make money is Krishna Consciousness. That is business. All pure devotees that is a business. So they are Dhani and Arapati. Is that a contradiction? That is the world of devotees. So, parityaag is not poverty. Parityaag is opulence.”

Parityaga is not poverty; it is opulence — one of Krishna's six opulences. Maharaj recalls Prabhupada telling Svarupa Damodara Maharaj, when the Bhaktivedanta Institute was being set up, to bring the budget without minimising anything: Krishna consciousness means money, not poverty. — “Renunciation is opulence.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:13 (auto-transcript): “parityaag is not poverty. Parityaag is opulence. Opulence. The six opulences of Krishna, one is renunciation. Which is opulence. Renunciation is opulence. Not poverty. And Prabhupada said, he was speaking to his own as Sarupadamudara Maharaj.”

children.topic: Christians have more faith than us
children.note: Christians say God is not poor, and they have that faith; Muslims too may have more faith than we do. We have big knowledge, scriptures, facilities and power in everything, yet our faith is small. Krishna states boldly in Gita 9.22 that he carries what his devotees lack and preserves what they have. — “The Christians they have more faith than us.”

children.topic: Q2 · Who were the buried books for?
children.note:
Govinda Prema Prabhu asks: Mahaprabhu told the Goswamis to write books to help us, yet some of their books lie in the Grantha Samadhi at Sanatana Goswami's samadhi, inaccessible to anyone. For whom were those written?

🎙 Maharaj at 42:27 (auto-transcript): “Thank you very much, sir. Gurudev, one of the assignments which Chaitanya Mahaprabhu gave to the Goswamis were to write books to help us. So I was curious about those books which were buried in Sanatana Goswami Samadhi. They pushed that Granth Samadhi is there. So those books…”

Maharaj's short answer: those books are not for us; they are for different people. — “They are not for us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:13 (auto-transcript): “They are not for us. They are for different people. So when they left, they have to send the bulls away. When Shamanand Pandit came to meet Shri Lajiva Goswami, here in Vrindavan, So, after training him, Shri Jeeva Goswami, he asked him a question.”

After training Syamananda Pandit and giving him his title, Jiva Goswami asks him why the trees of Vrindavan are dying despite plenty of rain and sun. Syamananda asks for time to consult — Maharaj explains that many systems of divination exist, with seeds or with ink. He returns with the answer: those trees came with Krishna and left when he left, their duty done; the one still standing was not planted by Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:34 (auto-transcript): “When Shamanand Pandit came to meet Shri Lajiva Goswami, here in Vrindavan, So, after training him, Shri Jeeva Goswami, he asked him a question. My dear Shamanand Pandit, he gave him a title. Shri Jeeva Goswami says, see, all the trees, they are all dying. They are all dead.”

When Krishna came to Gokula everything became complete, and when he went he took it all back with him — including the books. He left behind the ones we need.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:29 (auto-transcript): “so when Krishna came here when Krishna came to Gokul Brindar what Gokul is Gokul He became complete. Everything. He lost everything from the here. When he's going, he always took all of them back. Including the books. He left the one we need to show us. And even this one they…”

Even of the books left here, who is reading them? Someone wants Ujjvala-nilamani — Maharaj says you cannot read that book; you will fall down. It was not written for you. — “You cannot read that book.”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:12 (auto-transcript): “I love to have a Ujjal Nilamani. You cannot read that book. You are going to fall down. You are reading. You fall down. Patan will be made for you. So, do you mean for what? So, who will you write for it? For God's sake, he has written for you.”

The morning class said Vyasadeva had three sons — Dhritarashtra, Sukadeva Goswami and Vidura. Then how does Maharaja Pandu come into the picture?

🎙 Maharaj at 50:18 (auto-transcript): “Gurudev, in the morning class, you mentioned that Vyasa Deva had three sons, namely, Dhritarashtra, Sakadeva Goswami and Vidura. But then, how Maharaj Pandu came into that visit? Pandu is from a different mother. Different father, not from the same father. Different father,…”

children.topic: A different mother, the same family
children.note:
Maharaj answers briefly: Pandu is from a different mother. He names Citrangada and Vicitravirya as brothers of the same family, and says Vyasadeva was brought in to continue the lineage. — “Pandu is from a different mother.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:32 (auto-transcript): “Pandu is from a different mother. Different father, not from the same father. Different father, sorry. Chitrangada, Vichitravirya. They are brothers. Different. The same family. To continue the lineage.”

children.topic: Q4 · How did Rupa and Sanatana depart?
children.note:
Kishori Mataji shares that she missed the walk to Sanatana Goswami's samadhi but went later and felt as if she had lived there for many years; today's katha fulfilled her wish to know him more. She asks how Rupa and Sanatana Goswami concluded their pastimes on earth.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:38 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj. Thank you so much for today. Katha first about Vedavyasa and about Sanatana Goswami yesterday I failed to come with you to Samadhi but still we reached it when we went there I was feeling like this much years but I was feeling like I want to know about…”

Both left the body here in Vrindavan, and their samadhis here are real.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:20 (auto-transcript): “Here, Vrindavan. Then left the body. Just short while before Shrivas Acharya came. Shrivas. Shrivas, no Shrivas, Shrivas Acharya. So, he met Gopal Bhatt Goswami and Jeeva Goswami. Rupa Goswami and Sanatana Goswami”

They departed shortly before Srinivasa Acarya reached Vraja. At Vishram Ghat in Mathura he heard all of Vrindavan lamenting the loss of its jewels, and he lamented so much that Rupa and Sanatana appeared to him: we are here, and the work will continue — take initiation from Gopala Bhatta Goswami. He went on to meet Gopala Bhatta and Jiva Goswami.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:31 (auto-transcript): “Just short while before Shrivas Acharya came. Shrivas. Shrivas, no Shrivas, Shrivas Acharya. So, he met Gopal Bhatt Goswami and Jeeva Goswami. Rupa Goswami and Sanatana Goswami So we have their samadhi's here.”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 18 · Species in the Universe

nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.136–138 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Mahaprabhu tells Rupa Gosvami he can give only a drop of the ocean of devotional service, and begins with the living entities: unlimited in number, in 8,400,000 species, spread through every element and every planet. Maharaj takes on the scientists who deny life elsewhere, explains subtle bodies, walks through the count of species, and shows that the human species, though the smallest, suffers most — and that following the acaryas' principles is what makes us human. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Mahaprabhu tells Rupa that devotional service cannot be described in full, so he will give only a synopsis of its symptoms — a single drop from an ocean whose length and breadth no one can measure. The verses are read in Hindi and English.

The verse states that unlimited living entities in 8,400,000 species wander throughout the universe. Maharaj reads the translation and purport, pausing on the point that this directly challenges scientists and philosophers who presume life exists only on this planet.
Maharaj points to Bhagavad-gita 2.24: the living entity is sarva-gata, all-pervading, which he explains to mean it can go anywhere — so there is no reason to restrict life to one planet.

Maharaj frames the whole verse as a challenge to the scientists and philosophers. Those who went to the moon and reported no life there simply contradict what the Vedic literature says.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:40 (auto-transcript): “this is a challenge to the scientists and the philosophers Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes.”

Maharaj teaches that living entities are sprayed across the whole brahmanda — some species here, some there, some outside — plants, trees, insects, and beings in fire and water alike.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:42 (auto-transcript): “They are sprayed everywhere, everywhere in the whole Brahmand. Some species here, some species there, some species outside. The same with plants and trees. Insects. They are spread all over the places. Vishnu Purana has the calculation. Everywhere you go,”

Maharaj says the Vishnu Purana gives the calculation of species, and quotes the line counting 900,000 aquatics. Wherever you go, even into fire, living entities are there.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:18 (auto-transcript): “Vishnu Purana has the calculation. Everywhere you go, in the fire, living entities are there. In the water, Varit is a living entity. Jalajjar Nagar Lakshani, 900,000 aquatics. They go to the ocean. So scientists went to the ocean, they didn't find Varuna.”

Scientists went down into the ocean and did not find Varuna, the presiding deity of the waters. Maharaj's answer is simple: Varuna is there; not finding him says nothing about his existence.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:55 (auto-transcript): “They go to the ocean. So scientists went to the ocean, they didn't find Varuna. Varuna is there. Even within our own experience There are no varieties of fish there in the water No In the water no varieties of fish Water entities are not only fish Snakes also live in the…”

Even from our own experience there are endless varieties in the water — not only fish but snakes and four-legged animals. Maharaj says people from the village know these things, while the scientists know nothing, and yet the world worships them. — “but scientists doesn't know anything”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:32 (auto-transcript): “Snakes also live in the water there are four-legged animals who live in the water varieties we from village we know these things but scientists doesn't know anything foolish people But the world is worshipping them. There are varieties of fishes in the water.”

Maharaj's analogy: if a scientist tells a fisherman there are no fish in the water, who will take him seriously? The fisherman catches fish every day. Saying there is no life on the moon means only that they did not actually go there.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:47 (auto-transcript): “If a scientist tells a fisherman No, but it's a fish in the water. Who will they look at him? Because they are catching fish every day, they are catching fish every day, so how can you say that they are not? They are everywhere, entities everywhere.”

children.topic: Qualification to be in a place
children.note:
To be in a particular place one needs the qualities for it. Maharaj says those claiming to have gone to the moon lacked the qualification, and so either did not go or could not perceive what is there. — “One has to have the qualities to be in a particular place.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:36 (auto-transcript): “One has to have the qualities to be in a particular place. So they don't have the qualifications to go there. They thought they did not go there. And there is a document, this is a document to prove that they didn't go there. They are just law of us. i say he killed him right…”

children.topic: Bodies of mind, intelligence, false ego
children.note:
Beings on other planets have forms made of different elements. Maharaj asks whether a gross person can see an entity whose body is made of mind, intelligence and false ego — no.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:31 (auto-transcript): “forms composed of different elements. The entities who have their body made of mind intelligence and force, will a gross person see? No. We say, disembodied beings, disembodied beings. Disembodied beings means they have a subtle body.”

What people call disembodied beings are not bodiless; they have a subtle body of mind, intelligence and false ego, only without the gross covering. — “Disembodied beings means they have a subtle body.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:57 (auto-transcript): “We say, disembodied beings, disembodied beings. Disembodied beings means they have a subtle body. Made of mind, intelligence and false ego. Not the gross one. They don't have the gross one. Remember? When Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appeared. And Demigod all came.”

Maharaj recalls that when Caitanya Mahaprabhu appeared, the demigods came to take darsan of the Lord. People sensed someone passing and called a priest to chant mantras to drive them off, while the demigods looked on and laughed.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:35 (auto-transcript): “When Chaitanya Mahaprabhu appeared. And Demigod all came. Oh. Take darsan of the Supreme Presity of Godhead. and sometimes people were noticing someone is passing here someone is passing so they call for a priest to come and chant mantra they sing a mantra was chanting the…”

In the same way, Maharaj says, the Vedic student laughs at the scientists and philosophers, because they are talking nonsense when they deny the varieties of beings living in the air without gross bodies. — “They will laugh at the scientists and the philosophers.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:12 (auto-transcript): “the student, the Vedic student, the Vedic student, They will laugh at the scientists and the philosophers. Because they are talking nonsense. There are varieties who live in the air. They don't have the gross element. when his soul leaves the gross body he sighs”

children.topic: The subtle body takes the punishment
children.note:
When the soul leaves the gross body it carries the subtle body of mind, intelligence and false ego, and that is the body taken to hell to undergo punishment. The gross body could not bear it; the subtle body does. So the Vedas are correct.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:49 (auto-transcript): “when his soul leaves the gross body he sighs the body made of my intelligence and falsely go that body we take to hell and we will be able to undergo the punishment The gross body would not take it. The subtle body would take it. So the Vedas are correct.”

Maharaj goes through the classical division of species, explaining each category and adding the figures up to eight million four hundred thousand.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:55 (auto-transcript): “There are 900,000 aquatics living in the water. There are also two million non-moving living entities. Stavara, Laksh, Bhimzati.”

Two million non-moving entities, the sthavara: those who stand in one place, that is, plants and trees.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:37 (auto-transcript): “Stavara, Laksh, Bhimzati. Stavara. Stavara. Yes. The entities who stand in one place. Plant and trees. There are also 1,100,000 species of insects and reptiles. And there are 1,000,000 species of birds. As far as quadruples and quadrupeds are concerned, there are 3,000,000…”

900,000 aquatics, 2,000,000 plants and trees, 1,100,000 insects and reptiles, 1,000,000 birds, 3,000,000 four-legged animals, and 400,000 human species — eight million four hundred thousand in all.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:03 (auto-transcript): “There are also 1,100,000 species of insects and reptiles. And there are 1,000,000 species of birds. As far as quadruples and quadrupeds are concerned, there are 3,000,000 varieties, that is animals. 1 million is birds 1 million 100 is insects Reptiles That is 8 million”

Maharaj draws attention to the fact that the human species, at 400,000, is the smallest of all the categories. — “So human species is the smallest”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:52 (auto-transcript): “There are 400,000 human species So human species is the smallest and they are the ones who have trouble the most animals don't have starvation starvation is only with the human species nor the moon he said he has troubled the whole He was associated with all species of life.”

children.topic: The smallest species, the most trouble
children.note:
Though fewest in kind, human beings are the ones in the most trouble. Maharaj contrasts us with the animals, who do not suffer the problems we create for ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:01 (auto-transcript): “and they are the ones who have trouble the most animals don't have starvation starvation is only with the human species nor the moon he said he has troubled the whole He was associated with all species of life. And his experience is that the most miserable of all are human…”

Animals do not have starvation; starvation belongs to the human species alone. Maharaj cites the experience of one who associated with all species of life and found human beings the most miserable. — “starvation is only with the human species”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:06 (auto-transcript): “animals don't have starvation starvation is only with the human species nor the moon he said he has troubled the whole He was associated with all species of life. And his experience is that the most miserable of all are human beings.”

We, the 400,000 species, are the ones talking about overpopulation; no one speaks of overpopulation or poverty among the three million animal species. Maharaj asks what explains this, and answers: karma.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:55 (auto-transcript): “We are the ones who talk about overpopulation. I can give you overpopulation for 100,000 and not 3 million. No, overpopulation for 3 million. Overpopulation for 400,000. Stabation for 400,000. Poverty. 400,000. There is no property for animals. What is that?”

children.topic: Purana — the soul is always old
children.note:
From the Gita's word purana, Maharaj explains that the soul is very old, never new. When we look at a baby and call it new, we are seeing only the body.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:38 (auto-transcript): “means very old, not new, not new, what is new, when they say baby, what are you looking at, baby, not the body, not the soul, the soul is purana, but the body is new baby new baby is old this old man not new nothing is new the body is”

The body is new or old, but the soul is always old. The baby is an old soul in a new body; nothing about the self is new. — “but the soul is always old”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:00 (auto-transcript): “but the body is new baby new baby is old this old man not new nothing is new the body is new and old but the soul is always old for the soul there is neither birth nor death”

Bhagavad-gita 2.20: the soul has no birth and no death, it never came into being and never will, and it is not slain when the body is slain. Maharaj adds the Hindi: the jivatma is both ananta and anadi.

Among the 400,000 human species, Maharaj says, many have sankucita — constricted — consciousness, not open, like trees and plants. Even within humans the consciousness is not yet fully human.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:28 (auto-transcript): “So within the 400,000. wouldn't this 100,000 we have sankuchita constricted constricted consciousness consciousness is not open Like trees and plants. Even within humans. So means 200,000 is of human.”

Sankucita means constricted: consciousness that is not open. Maharaj applies the word not only to plants but to a large part of the human species.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:40 (auto-transcript): “sankuchita constricted constricted consciousness consciousness is not open Like trees and plants. Even within humans. So means 200,000 is of human. Within the 400,000 human.”

children.topic: The acaryas' principles make us human
children.note:
Because we lack the qualities of a human being, our acaryas gave us principles to keep in order to make us human. They are not a punishment; they are meant for freedom. — “They are meant for freedom.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:42 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, our achara gave us principles to keep, to make us human beings. So, intelligent persons should keep to these principles. They are not punishment. They are meant for freedom. So, should keep these principles. Joyfully. So be free.”

Intelligent persons keep these principles, and keep them joyfully — and so become free.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:13 (auto-transcript): “So, should keep these principles. Joyfully. So be free. A man's, even within a species, we find that a father's consciousness is different from his son's”

Closing the purport, Maharaj restates the law of transmigration: we move from one body to another according to our consciousness, as a father's consciousness differs from his son's and a child's from a youth's. He ends early to attend a meeting.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:08 (auto-transcript): “We change from one body to another in terms of our consciousness. Salafabhupadiki. Yeah. All right. I have to go for my meeting. I will see you tomorrow. Hare Krishna. Hare Krishna.”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 19 · Can We Measure the Size of the Soul?

nodeData.topic: Day 19 · Can We Measure the Size of the Soul?
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.139–142 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The soul is one ten-thousandth of the tip of a hair, yet that spark runs an ant and runs Brahma, and builds aircraft. Maharaj draws out the lesson: our body and situation come from our own desires, so use this life to earn a spiritual body, and surrender. The Q&A covers why comfort makes practice hard, whether suffering is Krishna's plan or our karma, rigid sadhana without holidays, preaching to oneself, and whether a liberated soul remembers its past. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Today: how small is the soul?
children.note: Maharaj continues Madhya-lila chapter 19 from text 139, where Mahaprabhu tells Sanatana Gosvami the dimension of the living entity. The verses are read with Hindi translation.

children.topic: 19.139 — One ten-thousandth of a hair tip
children.note: The verse gives the measure of the soul: divide a hair tip into a hundred, and one of those into a hundred again. Srila Prabhupada's purport ties it to Bhagavad-gita 15.7, where Krishna calls the living entities his eternal fragments.

children.topic: Can anyone split a hair tip?
children.note:
Maharaj asks the room: take a piece of hair, not your long hair, and cut it into a hundred. Can anyone do it? Someone says scientists can. Then how will you take one piece out and divide that again? We do not have that power, but Krishna does.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:19 (auto-transcript): “If we divide the tip of a hair into a hundred parts, can anyone do that? Scientists can do it. Not your long hair Not your long hair Just a piece of the hair You cut it into one hundred And can you do that? Anyone can do that? Then how will you take one piece out of it?”

children.topic: Krishna tells us our own size
children.note:
Krishna gives this measure so that we understand what we are: so insignificant that we cannot even be calculated materially. Only Krishna could measure us, and he did.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:25 (auto-transcript): “So for us, Krishna is trying to let us understand how important we are, Hare Krishna. But so important, So great that we are very insignificant, very insignificant, but we are bewildered by illusion. To think that we are six feet tall, five point eight.”

children.topic: Six feet tall is an illusion
children.note:
To think I am five foot eight or six feet is illusion. We are tiny, and bewildered by identification with the body.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:08 (auto-transcript): “To think that we are six feet tall, five point eight. that is an illusion we are not 5 feet, 6 feet or 50 point something very insignificant very insignificant yet because we are spiritual spark of Krishna this is the priests We can create a mighty Boeing aircraft.”

Because we are sparks of Krishna, that tiny particle can design a mighty aircraft and fly it far above the sea. That capacity is spirit, not matter. — “We can create a mighty Boeing aircraft.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:45 (auto-transcript): “because we are spiritual spark of Krishna this is the priests We can create a mighty Boeing aircraft. They will fly it is 37,000 kilometers above the sea level. That is spirit.”

Maharaj dwells on the purport's point that one atomic portion of spirit can be the biggest brain in the material world. The same spark is in an ant and in Brahma, and Brahma's brain, big as an elephant, is made of the same twenty-four elements as the ant's. Yet Brahma's soul is still one ten-thousandth of a hair tip.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:44 (auto-transcript): “Spiritual strength is so powerful that the main atomic portion of spirit can be the biggest brain in the material world. the size of an insignificant”

Everyone's tongue is made of the same elements, yet our tastes differ, because the quantity and quality of the mixture differ. That is how Brahma's intelligence differs from ours while the soul stays the same size.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:37 (auto-transcript): “See, looking at the Brahman's intelligence, All of us have different tastes. But our tongue contains the same elements. The elements are the same. But the quantity of this and the quality differs. That's the Brahma's position. And it's a tiny entity.”

If the tiny soul has such strength, how can we hope to grasp the mighty Supreme Person by our own effort? Maharaj answers: we can understand him only by his mercy. — “We can understand him only by his mercy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:56 (auto-transcript): “so if we can do this what about a mighty, supreme presence of God. How do we hope to understand such person? We can understand him only by his mercy. See, looking at the Brahman's intelligence,”

children.topic: We are limited, he is unlimited
children.note:
Brahma is a tiny entity with enormous capacity; the Lord is unlimited, ananta. That contrast between limited and unlimited is what spirit means.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:18 (auto-transcript): “And it's a tiny entity. What about the muscle of Brahma? Unlimited. Anand. We are limited but he is unlimited. That is spirit. The spiritual strength is so powerful that a main atomic portion of spirit can be the biggest brain in the material world. The same spiritual spark…”

children.topic: Body and birth come from desire
children.note:
The different bodies, species and places we are born into all rest on our own desires. Our next situation is set by our present activities. If someone is high and someone low, it is not Krishna who did it; it is we who wanted positions. — “all are based on our desires”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:23 (auto-transcript): “the different bodies which we have different species which we are placed in geographical considerations all are based on our desires our desires has given us where we are now. Our next situation is also determined by our present activities.”

Understanding this, we can plan a next life better than this one. Not understanding it, we grow envious of others, complicate our situation, and the next life is worse.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:22 (auto-transcript): “this will be clearly understood because if we know this we will plan the next life to be better than the present one if we don't understand this we will implicate ourselves more by becoming envious of others will complicate the situation and the next life will be worse than…”

children.topic: Rsabhadeva: a big mistake already made
children.note:
Maharaj cites the advice of Lord Rsabhadeva: accepting the body we now have was already a great mistake, so an intelligent person does not use this body to earn another material body.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:09 (auto-transcript): “so Lord Buddha Savadev has given us advice we have already made a very big mistake accepting the body we have now a big mistake an intelligent person should not use this body to get another material body advancement means we are using the present body to get a better body”

Advancement is using the present body to get the special body that takes us back to Godhead. If you see someone intelligent, it means he is working for a spiritual body next life. That is why we study scripture: it lets us modify our activities so that spiritual life succeeds.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:41 (auto-transcript): “advancement means we are using the present body to get a better body that is called success get a special body that will take us back home back to Godhead if you see someone is intelligent means the person is working for a spiritual body in next life that's the importance of…”

A second scriptural statement of the same dimension, dividing the hair tip twice. Maharaj notes that the first lines come through the Pancadasi from Svetasvatara Upanisad 5.9, one of the chief Vedic mantras.

children.topic: 19.141 — Among the subtle, I am the jiva
children.note: Krishna's own words from Srimad Bhagavatam 11.16.11: he identifies himself with the living entity, who is one in quality with him and yet the smallest of the small while he is the biggest of the big.

We are all Krishna's parts, amsa, and eternal as he is. But here we are in a different situation: conditioned, controlled by another energy, without freedom. Our freedom exists only with Krishna. — “Our freedom is only with Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:12 (auto-transcript): “Krishna identifies himself with us, the living entities. Krishna is saying that all these things are the same in life. Krishna is saying that all of us are his part, Amsa are his part. we are all eternal”

children.topic: The point of it all: surrender
children.note:
These instructions are given so we can see our situation clearly. The conclusion is to surrender completely to Krishna and be delivered from the grip of material nature. — “we are meant to surrender ourselves completely to Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:56 (auto-transcript): “So, we are getting the instructions so we can understand our situation. At the end, we are meant to surrender ourselves completely to Krishna. There is the idea of this instruction. If we surrender to Krishna, and become delivered from the clutches of material nature. Hare…”

Five questions from the audience, several asked in both English and Hindi.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:38 (auto-transcript): “Comments, questions? Yeah, question. Thank you, Shri. I have a question from Deshares. I see that when there's difficulty At that time, it's easier to pray and take care of the scriptures. But when these difficulties are not there, at that time, it's more tough to focus and…”

children.topic: Q1 · Prayer is easy in trouble, hard in comfort
children.note:
In difficulty it is easy to pray and turn to scripture; when life is peaceful it is hard to practise intensely. How to practise with intensity when there are no difficulties?

🎙 Maharaj at 29:55 (auto-transcript): “Thank you, Shri. I have a question from Deshares. I see that when there's difficulty At that time, it's easier to pray and take care of the scriptures. But when these difficulties are not there, at that time, it's more tough to focus and pray intensely. So, in that situation,…”

Maharaj's blunt answer: a devotee with no challenges is not advancing. He is sleeping soundly on the lap of Maya. — “A devotee who has no challenges is not making an advancement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:52 (auto-transcript): “A devotee who has no challenges is not making an advancement. He is sleeping sound on the lap of Maya. Kunti Devi is not a fool she's not pretending”

Queen Kunti was no fool and was not pretending. She asked Krishna for more problems, because problems made her call on him constantly, and when she called he was with her. So if we have no challenges, Maharaj says, ask for them.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:28 (auto-transcript): “Kunti Devi is not a fool she's not pretending she was sure what she's doing she said but Krishna give me more problems because problems help me to call on you and to constantly calling on you I am always with you”

Maharaj recalls a disciple reporting many temple problems and the guru replying, very good; had everything been fine, he would have created a problem himself. Maharaj adds that the first time in his life he went to the police and to court was after he became a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:39 (auto-transcript): “Prabhu, how is your temple? So Gurudev saw most problem Gurudev said that's very good If he had told me that everything is fine Paul, I've created one problem for you. Want to be his disciple? Do you want to take an instruction from him? When he's dancing, I smell it. This is…”

children.topic: Looking for a cool room in a burning house
children.note:
His guru told him: you are a fool, living in a burning house and looking for a room to sleep peacefully. Whatever room you pick, the fire reaches it. The intelligent thing is to get out. Where is peace in this world? Anyone looking for it here is a fool. — “So anyone who is looking for peace is a fool.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:25 (auto-transcript): “he told me, you are a fool. You are living in a burning house and you want to find a war room and sleep peacefully there. Will you sleep peacefully there? How long will you sleep there? The house is on fire. Any room you take to sleep in, the fire will get there. Is that…”

To the follow-up about stopping practice and returning: you restart from where you left off. Our past piety was small, so our interest in Krishna was small; we take Maya's punches, make offences, leave, come back, many times. What was practised is not erased. Keep going and you grow stronger and eventually succeed.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:22 (auto-transcript): “If you stop practicing, that was the question, you stop practicing for the time being, then you come back. Yes, you make advancement from where you start. For us to come to Christian consciousness. We have had a lot of ups and downs. Because our previous poverty is very small.”

children.topic: Q2 · Krishna's plan or my karma?
children.note:
When a devotee faces difficulty, how to tell whether it is the Lord testing and teaching, or simply the fruit of one's own desires and karma?

🎙 Maharaj at 40:14 (auto-transcript): “is asking the difficulties. So in the devotee lives, if you face difficulty, how to differentiate that it's God's plan, or it's our karma, desire, that life we are suffering. In the devotee life also. How to differentiate God is testing and God is looking at this depression…”

children.topic: A sincere sadhaka is in Krishna's hands
children.note:
For a devotee chanting sixteen rounds daily, avoiding offences, keeping discipline and a fixed service, whatever happens is arranged by Krishna directly, not by Durga. Such a fortunate devotee says: Krishna, thank you.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:43 (auto-transcript): “The devotee who is chanting Siksniyran daily. Trying to avoid offenses Keeping the effort and good discipline”

From the purports to Bhagavad-gita 12.13–14: a devotee in distress takes it as the Lord's mercy. He never asks, Krishna, why me, are you really God? He thinks: for my past misdeeds I should suffer far more; by his mercy I get only a little. So he stays calm, quiet and patient.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:27 (auto-transcript): “Whenever a devotee is in distress or has fallen into difficulty Is Bhagavad Gita chapter 12, text 13 and 14 purports He thinks that it is the Lord's mercy upon him. A devotee does say, Krishna, why am I suffering like this? Why? I'm so pure.”

A neophyte's position is said to be dangerous because he does not know how to deal with others. How does one rise from kanistha to madhyama?

🎙 Maharaj at 46:29 (auto-transcript): “So if you could just elaborate more on how does one of the neophytes place to the level of Madhyama. So, now my question is that Shavadir says that if a non-seekhya bhakt or a new bhakt, tanish bhakt is very dangerous and dangerous because we don't know how to deal with it.…”

Maharaj's answer is two words repeated: rigid practice. No compromise. That is the way to advance.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:20 (auto-transcript): “Rigid practice. Rigid practice. No compromise. That is the way for advancement. Today I'm not going to work. So I can wake up by 6 o'clock.”

He mimics the mind: today I am not working, so I will wake at six instead of three, I can chant later. No. Mangala-arati is at the same hour every day. Prabhupada's phrase is not falling down in all circumstances: no break, no recreation, no holiday, fixed. By constant practice we transcend the modes. — “Brahma Muhurta doesn't have holiday.”

We are practising what we will do eternally with Krishna, and Krishna takes no day off from the cows. Even when Mother Yasoda told him not to go to the forest, he went. That is the strength of following one's dharma.

Waking every day, you say you are tired. It is not you; the body and the mind are tired. The spirit soul is cetana, conscious, and nitya, eternal. — “It's a question of tiredness, the body, the mind, not the soul.”

When we preach, the first person we address is the self. Maharaj's example: if someone announces that all devotees should come tomorrow, the first person we look for in the morning is the one who made the announcement. children.topic: From vaidhi to raga, gross to subtle
children.note:
