maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 20 · Our So-Called Advancement in Science

nodeData.topic: Day 20 · Our So-Called Advancement in Science
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.143–144 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Living entities exist everywhere — in earth, water, air and even fire — each with a body suited to its element, and they are unlimited in number, divided into the moving and the non-moving. Maharaj uses the frog in the well to show why scientists, philosophers and politicians cannot measure the unlimited, and insists that real knowledge comes from the Vedas and the acaryas. A question on why devotees should study the universal form leads to the Vrajavasis who wanted only the two-handed son of Nanda. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 19.143 — Living entities everywhere, even in fire
children.note: The recording opens inside the purport, where Gita 2.24 is being read: the soul cannot be cut, burned or dried, so living beings can exist in any element. Mahaprabhu's verse says the living entities are found all over the universe, in every kind of body.

children.topic: A body fit for its element
children.note:
Maharaj asks the room what the bodies of those living in fire are made of — not earth, not water, but fire, ether and air — so they live there as peacefully as fish live in water. Our body is predominantly earth, so earth is where we are comfortable. The sun-god lives in fire quite comfortably.

🎙 Maharaj at 02:29 (auto-transcript): “living entities are there their body does not have an element does it have water element the body is made of fire ether and air so they can live peacefully in the fire like the sun god”

Go to the watery region and tell all the fish and aquatics that there is no place but water: they will believe you, because water is all they have ever seen. This sets up the frog story.

🎙 Maharaj at 04:09 (auto-transcript): “if you go to the watery region apart from Varunadev and he tells all the fish and all the varieties of aquatics there is no other place except water there is no other place except water they will believe they will believe you they will believe that there is no other place…”

Maharaj tells the classic story: a frog from the ocean visits a frog in a small well and invites him to come and see a bigger body of water. The well-frog can only ask — two of this size? three? — because 'unlimited' does not exist in his dictionary.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:05 (auto-transcript): “a frog in a small well so another frog from the ocean prayed the visit and they were discussing so the friend from the ocean said I would like you to come and visit me You see a bigger body of water than this one. What? What? You get on this? How big is that?”

Maharaj asks what the ocean frog thinks of his friend: not that he is lying, but that he is ignorant — a foolish friend trying to calculate the ocean with his own limited ability. What is his qualification to measure the ocean's water?

🎙 Maharaj at 06:02 (auto-transcript): “What the frog from the ocean would be thinking about the frog in the world? Who is he thinking? Not lie. Ignorance. This is my foolish friend. He doesn't know anything. want to calculate the ocean by its own limited ability what is the qualification to calculate the water in…”

Speak to Varuna about the ocean and he knows exactly what it is; he has the bigger facility and intelligence. When we say 'ocean' we mean unlimited, but for the frog only the limited exists.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:46 (auto-transcript): “but if you tell Baruna about ocean it's fine what it is He has a bigger facility intelligence to understand when we say ocean what are we looking at? When we say ocean what are we looking at? Unlimited It's unlimited It's unlimited Unlimited ocean”

For Mahaprabhu and the Gita it is not difficult to say that living entities are everywhere, moving and non-moving. Our job is to hear from them rather than measure from inside our well. — “So we should not be like a frog in the well.”

🎙 Maharaj at 08:35 (auto-transcript): “So it's not difficult for them to understand. So we should not be like a frog in the well. Our scientists are frog in the well. Because they don't have the brain to understand how unlimited is Krishna. So they should consult the Vedas. and the acharyas, then they can…”

children.topic: Scientists are frogs in the well
children.note:
Maharaj applies the story directly: our scientists are frogs in the well, lacking the brain to grasp how unlimited Krishna is. They should consult the Vedas and the acaryas; otherwise there is no question of understanding.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:47 (auto-transcript): “Our scientists are frog in the well. Because they don't have the brain to understand how unlimited is Krishna. So they should consult the Vedas. and the acharyas, then they can understand, otherwise there is no question of understanding. In the material world, our advancement…”

What does advancement mean in the material world? Maharaj answers that what we call progress is only an expansion of ignorance — still ignorance, however big it grows. — “It is not advancement, it is still expansion of ignorance.”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:24 (auto-transcript): “In the material world, our advancement means what? Advancement is what we are preparing for, how do we make this expansion of ignorance? It is still ignorance. It is not advancement, it is still expansion of ignorance. We are considering this advancement. What is advancement?”

He died — burst trying to imagine the ocean. In the same way, Maharaj says, the froggy scientist who tries to understand Krishna with a limited brain is dead; he repeats the word 'dead' for effect.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:39 (auto-transcript): “What happened to the frog in the world? He died. The same way, a froggy scientist you are dead dead froggy scientists dead thinking to understand Krishna dead how many of you have read”

Asked what advancement is, the room offers 'skyscrapers'. Maharaj replies that a skyscraper here is only the reflection of what is in Vaikuntha, and the reflection looks identical to the original — you cannot see the difference, because the original is real.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:10 (auto-transcript): “Skyscrapers. What is it? Skyscrapers and Vekuntha. What is it? Skyscrapers and Vekuntha and the reflection of the skyscraper in Vaikuntha. The reflection, the reflection, the reflection of a skyscraper in Vaikuntha is the same.”

children.note:
Maharaj cites an acarya: when new devotees reach Vaikuntha the older residents laugh, because the newcomers cannot tell the real building from its shadow, while the old devotees know which is the true beauty. The ocean frog laughs at the well frog in the same way.

Maharaj asks how many have read Brahma-samhita and what they understood. Most know only one line. He presses: what is the quadrangle, the triangle described there? Silence.

Mahaprabhu continues: the living entities are unlimited and fall into two divisions, the moving and the non-moving.

Maharaj asks: are we unlimited? Someone answers 'a number', which is what he wanted. Each of us is a limited living entity; it is the count across the universes that is unlimited. — “The unlimited here is not our size, it's the number.”

The Padma Purana gives the number of species of plants and trees as two million, and they are not all on this planet — they are spread across the universe, some here, some there.

Mahaprabhu gives the training: the moving beings are birds, beasts and aquatics; the non-moving are plants, trees and mountains. Maharaj remarks that mountains once moved but are now stationary. This is what the Padma Purana says, and we are simply repeating it.

The conclusion of the class: our knowledge should come from the Vedas, not from scientists, philosophers or politicians. With scripture we are complete. — “So we should take our knowledge from the Vedas.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:42 (auto-transcript): “So we should take our knowledge from the Vedas. not from the scientists please not from the philosophers please not from the philosophers not from scientists not from politicians these three people are dangerous take our knowledge from the scriptures then we are complete with…”

Maharaj names scientists, philosophers and politicians as three classes of people who are dangerous as sources of knowledge, repeating 'please' as he rules each out.

The beauty of studying scripture is that it tells us exactly where we are in the universe, what the supreme position of God is, and what our relationship with him is.

Maharaj closes with the Isopanisad's definition: the scripture that brings the living entity close to the Supreme Lord by destroying ignorance and revealing our identity is called Upanishad.

children.topic: Q1 · Why study the universal form at all?
children.note:
In the Second Canto Prabhupada calls Narada's mind a frog in the well when he thinks Brahma is all-powerful. If so, why do we need to know the universal form, the Vaikuntha and Goloka charts, Ksirodakasayi Visnu and the rest?

children.topic: For us, not for pure devotees
children.note:
Maharaj answers that pure devotees do not need any of it; it is there to convince people like us that there is somebody supreme. — “It is necessary to convince us that there is somebody supreme there.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:15 (auto-transcript): “It is not necessary for pure devotees. It is necessary to convince us that there is somebody supreme there. Pure devotee is not necessary.”

When Krishna showed the Vrajavasis Vaikuntha and his four-armed form, their pain only increased — they called it a nightmare. He removed it and returned to two hands, and they thanked him: even a short while without their Krishna was painful. — “we don't want that nightmare again”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:02 (auto-transcript): “When Krishna should the universe have formed the Vrajabhasis they were in pain. What is this? Krishna took them to Vaikuntha. your pain increased he showed them 400 oh what is he doing it's a nightmare it's a nightmare seeing the anxiety and Krishna removed all that”

The boys told Krishna that when he hides behind a tree during their games they feel unbearable pain for that moment — so what will they do when he goes to Mathura for days? Such devotees have no need of four hands. Maharaj notes that some of us sitting here feel no pain of separation at all, which is why we need these teachings to make us look for Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:40 (auto-transcript): “The cowhead boys they told Krishna Krishna when we are playing with you in the course of our play when you just run behind a tree you will feel so much pain for this short moment. Now, when you go to Mathura what will you do? Think of it. Pain. The Christians were there, they…”

When the gopis searching for Krishna met him in his Narayana form, they offered respect and asked only for the blessing of finding the son of Nanda Maharaja. They had no business with Narayana. So, Maharaj concludes, this knowledge is for non-devotees, not for devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:44 (auto-transcript): “when gopis were looking for Krishna And Krishna showed him beforehand. Oh Narayan. Blessings to you. Can you show us when the son of Mahārādanda passed? Can you show us when the son of Mahārādanda passed? Can you give us blessing to get the son of another Mahārādanda? That's…”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 21 · Uncultured People are Everywhere

nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.145–146 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Civilisation is a matter of consciousness, not of country or birth: cultured and uncultured people are found everywhere. Maharaj shows that the most powerful demons are those who speak religion but use it for themselves, that Mahaprabhu deliberately raised devotees from so-called low families, and that a preacher who discriminates geographically disqualifies himself. Q&A on why people avoid devotees, on Vrtrasura and Indra, and on the human species across the universe. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Continuing the count of species, this verse says that even the small human division is further subdivided, because it contains many uncultured people such as mlecchas, pulindas, bauddhas and sabaras. Read with Hindi translation.
The verse distinguishes those who follow Vedic principles from those who only claim to, while acting against them. Maharaj reads the purport twice over and keeps returning to it through the class.

Maharaj stresses that 'civilised' here is not a country or a species. It is a state of consciousness, and both civilised and uncivilised people are spread across the whole universe. — “Civilized and uncivilized people are spread all over.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:46 (auto-transcript): “This is based on the country. This country, species, it is not because this is spread all over the universe. Civilized and uncivilized people are spread all over.”

Vedic civilisation begins from the sudra. Those below — mleccha, pulinda, bauddha, sabara, abhira, khasa — are not confined to one land; Maharaj says you find them everywhere you look.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:35 (auto-transcript): “Vedic Civilizations start from Sudra. Below the Sudra, like Mlechha, Pulinda, Bodha, Shabara, Abheera, Casas are spread all over.”

What separates the cultured from the uncultured is a single principle: our understanding of who God is and what our relationship with him is. Acting on that relationship is what Maharaj calls knowledge, or religion.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:31 (auto-transcript): “With a principal distinction. Our understanding about who is God. What is our relationship with God? That is the distinction. The word Vedah means knowledge.”

children.topic: Who are the most powerful demons?
children.note:
Maharaj asks the room a 'funny question' and makes them promise not to be angry: who are the most powerful demons in the world? The answers come — subtle ones, gross ones — and he leads them to his own: those who speak religion but do not follow it. — “So I ask you one funny question.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:10 (auto-transcript): “So I ask you one funny question. How will you not be angry with me? Promise me. The point is to open our eyes so we can see. Around the whole universe, the whole world, the most powerful demons, who are the most powerful demons? The most powerful demons, the most powerful…”

Those who use religion as a means of livelihood and maintenance are the most powerful demons. Maharaj names the type: the motivated teacher.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:39 (auto-transcript): “Then, those who use religion as a means for living, for maintenance, okay? Very good. Papaji is saying that the people who use the religion for their own practice is a powerful master. Motivated teachers. He is a motivated teacher. He is a motivated teacher.”

The great demons of scripture were not sudras but born in brahmana families. So do not look at countries or castes; all over the world there are people who claim to be religious but are actually demons.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:28 (auto-transcript): “Hiranyakashipu, Ravana and Shishupal, they are Brahmanas, not Sutra, they are Brahmanas. Right? They are powerful demons. Brahmana family?”

Maharaj asks where the Bhagavatam's Tenth Canto opens: with ksatriyas acting as leaders but behaving as demons, so that Krishna had to be invited to come.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:03 (auto-transcript): “The beginner of Bhagatam. where does he begin where does he begin 10th kanto 10th kanto 10th kanto where does he begin shatriyas who are acting as leader but demons where does he begin 10th kanto then Krishna was invited to come”

All over the world there are people who belong to no religious organisation and yet whose character is better than that of many who do. Maharaj gives examples from his own family and from the Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:19 (auto-transcript): “All over the world you'll see, you'll see people who have never, who doesn't belong to any religious organization, but their character is better than those who belong to religion. One day, I had my mother telling my father from now onward,”

One day his mother told his father that from now on she wanted no more sex — finished, and that was it. She had never visited India or read the Bhagavatam; where did she get it? Her character was such. Do we have people like that today?

🎙 Maharaj at 22:52 (auto-transcript): “One day, I had my mother telling my father from now onward, I don't want sex again. Shiret Bhagavatam?”

A brahmana of Uttar Pradesh, still living with a prostitute in old age; the Yamadutas asked the Visnudutas what renunciation he had when he was doing that. Maharaj's point: read our scriptures properly and understand what is actually happening, instead of reading only the letters. — “Don't read alphabets.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:46 (auto-transcript): “Where did he get the knowledge from? Where did he get the knowledge from? And where did he get the knowledge from? And where did he get the knowledge from? Brahman, no? And? And? And he was still living with a pursuit at what age? He was a Brahman in Uttar Pradesh, and in…”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura sent sannyasis to London and they came back without making devotees. Srila Prabhupada sent householders to the same place and they established Radha-Londonisvara. Maharaj asks: is that not a revolution?

🎙 Maharaj at 26:37 (auto-transcript): “Many people are thinking militias the first duty she went to London why did she succeed? Why did she succeed? Shla Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakon Sanyasiyo'n ko London bheja tha Unhain safalta nahin mili apne prachar karya mein Kya unhain bhakt banali Shla Prabhupat ki tara”

From the Hindi exchange: they did not have firm faith in the order of their guru. They decided it was not possible and went back.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:02 (auto-transcript): “Shla Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakon Sanyasiyo'n ko London bheja tha Unhain safalta nahin mili apne prachar karya mein Kya unhain bhakt banali Shla Prabhupat ki tara Why he didn't make Kya unhain bana pahai Prabhuji kehre hai ki unke andar eegdam dridh shraddha nahin thi…”

Where is Londonisvara? Among the very people the verse lists — mlecchas, yavanas, bauddhas. True or not? Maharaj asks.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:44 (auto-transcript): “In Londoneshwara is where? What is it? Where? Milichas. Milichas. Javanas. Bordas. True or not? I am talking to you, your preachers, you should open your eyes Otherwise, your preaching will not have effect”

Speaking directly to the preachers present: if you do not understand this, your preaching will have no effect on anyone's life, because you will discriminate geographically — and that is a disqualification. — “Otherwise, your preaching will not have effect”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:10 (auto-transcript): “I am talking to you, your preachers, you should open your eyes Otherwise, your preaching will not have effect If you don't understand these things You will not make any effect on people's life. Because you are going to discriminate geographically.”

Did you see what Caitanya Mahaprabhu was doing? Rupa and Sanatana, brahmanas, were placed in the Muslim government; Nityananda Prabhu was sent to Radhadesh. Maharaj says none of this was accidental — it was purposeful.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:14 (auto-transcript): “Don't you see what Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was doing? Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Did you see what he was doing? Did you see? Rupa Sanatana Goswami is with Brahmanas. Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu sent him to Muslim. It was purposeful. Right.”

Haridasa Thakura was born in a brahmana family; his parents left early and he was raised among Muslims. Maharaj says it was not as we usually think, and it was purposeful.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:26 (auto-transcript): “He sent Haridasa Sakura. Haridasa Sakura was born in Brahman. the Brahmana family His parents left early He migrated to a Muslim He was purposeful He was not directly born in a Muslim family like we think Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu”

Hanuman from an animal species, Prahlada from a demon family, Ramananda Raya a sudra kayastha who in Krishna's pastimes is Visakha sakhi — yet they rank with the Gosvamis. This is a teaching, Maharaj says, not degradation.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:16 (auto-transcript): “Hanuman Ji Pashuk Yoni Pralad Devonik family Did you see that? When he came He brought all of them from wherever Ramananda Rai Krishna Nila is what? Vishakh Vishakh Saki Chetanila Shutra Kaya Stha Kaya Stha Kaya Stha”

Vrindavan dasa Thakura explains that Mahaprabhu sends devotees into low families to make that place glorious, and Mahaprabhu himself told Haridasa Thakura that his birth was superior to his own. Externally we condemn these people; Mahaprabhu promoted them all. — “Devotees are everywhere.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:26 (auto-transcript): “What? Devotees are everywhere. Why? Why? Vrindavan Das Thakura said, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu send devotees to burial lines to make the place fatal. And Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu himself, He confirmed that. My dear Haridas Thakur Your birth is superior to mine”

children.topic: Who is mleccha, who is brahmana?
children.note:
One born in a mleccha family is chanting at six years old, and a brahmana is eating meat. So who is the mleccha and who is the brahmana? Is it happening or not?

🎙 Maharaj at 37:10 (auto-transcript): “His own one born in Malachya family. He is chanting six-year-old. And a Brahman is eating meat. Who is Malaysia? Who is Brahman? Is it happening or not? All the people who wanted to kill Narutam Das Chakura, they were all Brahmanas worshiping Durga. All the people who want to…”

children.topic: Why they wanted to kill Narottama
children.note:
Those who wanted to kill Narottama dasa Thakura were not mlecchas but brahmanas, worshippers of Durga. Maharaj asks what his offence was: he was teaching about God while they were not, living off the offerings instead. The envy says, you are doing what I am supposed to do, and you are exposing my deviation. — “You are doing what I'm supposed to do.”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:06 (auto-transcript): “They want to kill Narutam Daszakura. Who wanted to kill Narutam Daszakura? Who were the people? The militias. Who wanted to kill him? Who were they? Who were they? Who were the Brahman? No, Brahman asked.”

Maharaj asks whether brahmanas worshipping Durga is itself the problem — and answers that the fault lies with the brahmana, not with Durga.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:56 (auto-transcript): “Do the brahman worship Durga? Why do the brahman worship Durga? Why do the brahman worship Durga? The brahman worship is the brahman. It is not Durga. Is it not? It is not. The highest form of religion is that by which one becomes fully conscious of the existence of God,…”

The same envy appears among devotees: I do not want to see anyone doing what I cannot do, because it shows me my inability. If you stop, I feel comfortable. Maharaj asks us to recognise this in ourselves. — “I don't want to see anyone doing what I cannot do”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:08 (auto-transcript): “Some devotees, they feel that it's going to be close because I don't want to see anyone doing what I cannot do if you are not doing it I will be happy because you cannot be done But you are letting me to see my inability.”

A comment on why people avoid devotees, a comment on Vrtrasura and Indra that Maharaj develops at length, and a question on the human species.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:24 (auto-transcript): “Comments? Yes, sir. Hare Krishna Maharaj, the Lord. Thank you. Today, there are many people who are with those devotees who don't like to go and talk to them in their past. Because if they come with those devotees, there are a lot of restrictions on eating. That's my…”

children.topic: Q1 · People avoid devotees for the restrictions
children.note:
A devotee observes that many people do not want to mingle with ISKCON devotees because of our rules about eating and conduct. Maharaj's answer: if I come to you, you will show me where I am. Nobody wants to look into the mirror and see an ugly face. Unfortunate. — “Don't show me the mirror.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:40 (auto-transcript): “Today, there are many people who are with those devotees who don't like to go and talk to them in their past. Because if they come with those devotees, there are a lot of restrictions on eating. That's my question. Comment. Prabhuji has a comment to make that these days I've…”

children.topic: Q2 · Vrtrasura and Indra — who is the demon?
children.note:
A devotee recalls the acaryas' comment that in the fight between Vrtrasura and Indra, Vrtrasura, who taught self-realisation and wanted the Lord's lotus feet, should be called the sura, and Indra, who wanted to stay in the material world, the asura. Maharaj asks the room: so who is the demon?

🎙 Maharaj at 46:09 (auto-transcript): “In Srimad Bhagavatam, there is a fight between Vrithrasura and Indra, and Acharya is right in that commentary that Vrithrasura should be called as Asura, and Indra should be called as Sura Devata, but our Acharya write that in this episode where Vrithrasura was instructing on…”

Externally Vrtrasura is a demon, but look at his qualities. Pariksit Maharaja asked Sukadeva Gosvami how a demon could be so pure, and Sukadeva laughed — as the audience is laughing now.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:01 (auto-transcript): “Externally, Vritra Sur is a demon. But look at his quality. Parikshit Maharaj, I Shukadeva Goswami, this question. How can the demon be so simply? Shukadev Goswami was laughing like you are laughing. Right? He is supposed to be a demon but look how the activities are simply.…”

When Prthu Maharaja was performing his hundred sacrifices, Indra stole the horse in the disguise of a sannyasi and so introduced pakhanda, false religious orders. Who are Indra's representatives today? Those who do other things in the name of religion.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:49 (auto-transcript): “Do you remember when Prithu Maharaj was going to do the hundreds? Do you remember when Prithu Maharaj was going to do 100? Indra tried. He tried. He tried to be sure that it doesn't take place. He introduced Indra's religion.”

children.topic: Krishna spoke to Prthu, not Indra
children.note:
When Krishna came to settle the dispute, he did not address the one doing wrong; he spoke to the sinless Prthu, who could understand him, and Prthu stopped the sacrifice so that Indra could have peace. Prthu slept peacefully because he did what was right. — “Krishna didn't talk to Indra.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:39 (auto-transcript): “So, when Krishna came, two devotees were having issues. Indra. Demonic. Pritho Maharaj. Prayos. When Krishna came, whom did he speak to? Is he the one who is speaking to or the person who is doing activities, sinful activities? He is sinless.”

children.topic: Q3 · 400,000 human species — on earth only?
children.note:
Of the 8,400,000 species, are the 400,000 human forms only on this planet or across the planetary systems? Maharaj repeats the previous day's answer: the species are spread all over the universe, not in one place.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:08 (auto-transcript): “Out of the 84,000 spaces of living entities, the 400,000 are human beings. Does it limit to the human beings on the earthly planet or to the different planetary systems in the material world. So, Prabhu Ji, the question is that the 4,000,000 human beings are the ones in the…”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 22 · Who is Disqualified from Real Knowledge?

nodeData.topic: Day 22 · Who is Disqualified from Real Knowledge?
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.147 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Out of millions of karma-nisthas one becomes wise, and Maharaj asks why it takes so many births: the karmi and the jnani both move out of fear of suffering, not love of Krishna, so pious is not pure and oneness is only loneliness. Pious work is selfish, shown by King Nriga and by temples serving grains on Ekadasi. The class closes with a riddle: if Krishna compiled the Vedas, why did Mahaprabhu banish the Vedas personified from Mayapur? The four Vedas and the fifth Veda are two different things. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse says that among followers of Vedic knowledge most are fruitive workers judging good from bad work, and among many such sincere workers there may be one who is actually wise. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta's definition of karma-nistha is read in Hindi and English.

Maharaj asks the room how long it takes a karmi to become wise. The answer: many, many births. Why so many? Because they are pushed toward knowledge by frustration, not drawn by love. — “How long does it take karma nishtha or karmis to become wise?”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:00 (auto-transcript): “How long does it take karma nishtha or karmis to become wise? How long does it take karma nishtha or karmis to become wise? A whole janma. Many, many births. Why many births? they are taken to knowledge and to frustration”

Weighing good and bad karma brings a reserve of suffering, so the karmi decides to leave this platform and go higher. Maharaj stresses the motive: it is fear of suffering, not love for Godhead.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:03 (auto-transcript): “the process of cultivating activity and understanding distinguishing between good and bad karma brings negative reserve for suffering therefore I don't want to suffer so leave this platform and go higher out of fear of suffering”

Citing Kapila Muni, Maharaj says that service rendered out of fear of suffering belongs to the separatist category — one's own interest and Krishna's interest are still kept apart.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:00 (auto-transcript): “According to Kapila Muni. Devotional seva is bhakti out of fear of suffering. It's the category of separatist. The interest of Krishna The interest of Krishna Different It is different, but this devotional service is performed by a separatist.”

Bhakti is about the person being served, not my own consideration; if he is happy, my issue has nothing to do with it. Pure devotees pray: if your happiness requires my anxiety, give me more anxiety. Maharaj calls this very high, but says we must know it, otherwise we cannot walk towards it. — “Bhakti is not about my consideration.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:06 (auto-transcript): “Bhakti is different. Bhakti is not about my consideration. It's about the person whom I am offering this service to. If he is happy, Then, my issue has nothing to do with it. That is bhakti. So pure devotees.”

Krishna may call someone pious, but pious simply means good, not pure. Maharaj points to the Gita's twelfth chapter, where even pious activity is eventually given up.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:02 (auto-transcript): “But Krishna described me as pious. Pious does not mean pure. Pious simply means good. Not pure. So in chapter 12. Bhagavad Gita. Bhagavad Gita said. and pious activities will be given up. So, the distinction between good and bad work is what?”

Distinguishing between good and bad work is duality — what I like, what I dislike. Bhakti is above duality. — “Duality is not bhakti.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:43 (auto-transcript): “So, the distinction between good and bad work is what? Duality. Duality is not bhakti. Bhakti is superior to duality. What I like. Dislike. Good and bad duality. So they are above the karmi. But not the best.”

The jnani stands above the karmi but is not the best, because the monist position remains offensive to Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:19 (auto-transcript): “So they are above the karmi. But not the best. Because they are still offensive. That's still offensive. Towards the end of the set. This philosophy is called monism. O oneness. Ekattvam, that's oneness.”

The purport ends with monism, oneness, spiritual silence. Maharaj turns the word on the audience: what is one? Who here is one?

🎙 Maharaj at 17:47 (auto-transcript): “This philosophy is called monism. O oneness. Ekattvam, that's oneness. Yes. Oneness. Oneness. What is oneness? What is one? What is one?”

children.topic: Alone in the room for a hundred years
children.note:
Maharaj asks for one volunteer to stay in this room alone — not for a minute, for a hundred years — owning everything in it. Nobody wants it. Oneness means no interaction, just you, and that is suffering. — “Oneness means no interaction.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:39 (auto-transcript): “Who is one of us here? I want to see one person. I want to see one person. Who will stay in this room? alone. Everybody out. Only you stay here. Not for a minute. Not for a minute. For a hundred years. You have everything. Everything belongs to you. Everything belongs to you.…”

Maharaj recalls Radhanath Swami telling of a friend's son with two thousand toys, and how a child plays happily with a few. Our universe is made of 24 elements; we deal with the same 24 things for a whole life, and their quality only decreases. That is why nobody is happy here despite serious attempts.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:00 (auto-transcript): “Your entire life, you have only 24 items, for life, only 24 items. Do you be happy? Only 24 things. And I heard Parappuji Radhanath Swami Maharaj said that he has a friend, his son has 2,000 toys. 2,000 toys. I heard Parappuji Radhanath Swami Maharaj said that he has 2,000 kilos.”

We leave karma because it is gross suffering and move to the subtle platform, which is also suffering — the same thing in a finer form, and in fact more offensive. Merging, becoming God, only one God: where is the enjoyment?

🎙 Maharaj at 22:39 (auto-transcript): “We are leaving karma because it brings suffering. It's gross. We are going to the subtle platform which is also suffering what do they might descend one is gross one is subtle but they are the same in fact they are more offensive than they gross they are more offensive they…”

children.topic: Pious work does not take one home
children.note:
Pious men earn money with hardship and open charities, schools and hospitals. Maharaj grants it is good in one sense, especially if it leads to Krishna consciousness; otherwise it does not qualify one to go back to Godhead. — “pious activity does not qualify one to go back to Godhead”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:02 (auto-transcript): “They think that they are doing something good. In one sense, it's okay. It's good. Especially, if they are good work, lead them to Krishna consciousness. Then it is good. Otherwise, pious activity does not qualify one to go back to Godhead if pious activity”

If piety were enough, one person would be first back to Godhead. Krishna shows otherwise through a pastime: Maharaj Nriga introduced himself to Krishna by his charity — as countless as sand grains or showers of rain — and the result was a lizard's body in a dry well.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:39 (auto-transcript): “Who is that? Yes. Maharaj Nirga. Do you remember how he introduced himself to Krishna? My dear Lord Krishna. In the list of charitable personalities. you will find my name because my charity is like the farm at a sea show or the showers”

The performers of pious work are not serving Krishna's interest but their own: promotion to heavenly planets for better sense gratification, that is all.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:17 (auto-transcript): “And the performance of pious work they are shellfish. Shellfish. It is not our interest they are doing the pious work. It is their own interest. Because by doing this, you are promoted to heavenly planet. Why? Better science gratification.”

Many work hard to open hospitals and free schools. Maharaj asks: you train a poor person, very good — and he becomes an accountant, an engineer, a meat-eater? What good is that? It is good only if done for Krishna. — “It is good only if it is done for Krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:57 (auto-transcript): “so many people working very hard to earn money open hospitals free schools and many other philanthropic activities to help people suppose you train a poor person that's very good We have trained a person to become a professional animal killer.”

Maharaj says he has seen it many times here in Vrindavan: on Ekadasi people happily and vigorously distribute grains, thinking it is pious work. He asks whether it is.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:03 (auto-transcript): “And I have said this many times, here in Vrindavan, I have seen, many times, on a Kadhashi day, they are happily and vigorously distributing grains. Is that Paiyar's deed? Giving grains? That's Paiyar's work. One grain of rice.”

Who lives in a grain of rice on Ekadasi? The papa-purusha. How many on one plate? Caitanya Mahaprabhu told his mother that grains should not be taken on that day even in a dream. Maharaj calls it a very dangerous life.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:45 (auto-transcript): “One grain of rice. Who lives there? who lives in the grain on the carousel pap purush pap purush if you have a plate how many pap purusha is there how many you can count you see what we are doing very dangerous life”

In one temple Maharaj saw sweet rice being served in small cups on Ekadasi; when he returned the plate was clean — distributed to congregational members because they eat rice at home anyway. Maharaj's reply: they also eat meat at home, should we add meat and alcohol? Is it our duty to facilitate wrong? The president called a meeting and agreed to stop. — “They also eat meat in their house.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:16 (auto-transcript): “I was in one temple and in the morning, I saw it was serving sweet rice in small small small cups. So I went to take care of my deities. When I came back, the whole plate was clean. So I asked the Vice President, What happened to the Vice President we were serving? We have…”

At another temple the shop was open on Ekadasi, full of grains, to earn money to maintain the temple. Maharaj begged the president to convince him that the temple would close if grains were not sold for two days a month. The president went quiet, then said they would stop.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:09 (auto-transcript): “in the second temple to another temple we were there in the temple in the Kadasi I showed their shop was the open so I was seeing So I went straight to the shop. So I picked one. I said, Prabhu, what is this? I said, grains. I said, what is today? Ekadashi. So you sell this…”

We call ourselves Krishna devotees, but how do we think and act as devotees? Krishna consciousness means being conscious of Krishna all the time, not sometimes. Srila Prabhupada said: you are not maintaining the temple, Srimati Radharani is — so nothing should be an impediment. — “But how devoted are we in Krishna consciousness?”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:14 (auto-transcript): “We are Krishna devotees But how devoted are we in Krishna consciousness? How do we think as devotees? How do we act as devotees? Krishna consciously means to be conscious of Krishna all the time. Not sometimes.”

We sit on the asana in the morning, read the Vaishnava calendar — today is Ekadasi — and a few hours later grains are open to the public. We wonder why devotees suffer; Krishna does not wonder, he knows our records. We should not ask Krishna why, we should ask ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:40 (auto-transcript): “And before we open the shop, before we open the shop, we have sat on Asana, even before that, before that, in the morning, I couldn't have a Vaisna calendar, today is a Kadasi. And then after a few hours Ekarashi preparation is open to the public, Ekarashi food, sorry, grains…”

Those who avoid fruitive work and fall silent to merge into the Absolute are called wise. Maharaj says they give up gross sense gratification but take up a subtle form of it — speculation to become one with Krishna, which is an offense. We are eternally servants; that position cannot be changed.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:16 (auto-transcript): “Why? Because they are leaving the special gratification. Why? Because there is a stool form of indra-tripti, but in fact, he is doing the stool form of indra-tripti or bhog. Speculation. Speculation. into Krishna to become one with Krishna and Krishna to become one with…”

How do we recognise one who has perfect knowledge? He becomes humble, renounces the material world and attaches to Krishna. You cannot find a knowledgeable person who is materially attached; if he is, he is not wise. — “It means he is not wise.”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:20 (auto-transcript): “So why this person is one who has realized is this How do you know this one who has perfect knowledge becomes humble and renounce the material world and attached to Krishna as a wise person. You cannot find a knowledgeable person who is materially attached.”

Maharaj recalls that Caitanya Mahaprabhu told the Vedas personified — those who hold that God has no form and no senses — that they are offensive and cannot stay in Mayapur: change your profession, become a devotee, then you can stay.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:22 (auto-transcript): “Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu He told in Vedas personified Vedas personified Vedas Vedas personified Vedas personified Vedas personified Vedas personified Shastranya Mahaprabhu Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Is all said You cannot stay in Mayapur You cannot stay in Mayapur Because you…”
Krishna says in the Gita that one who rejects the scriptural injunctions and acts on his own whim attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme destination.
Scripture is the breath of Krishna; he says he compiled the Vedas, he is knowledge, the object of knowledge and the one to be known. Maharaj deliberately sets this verse beside 16.23.

Maharaj's question to the room: Krishna gave the Vedas and says they are meant to know him — yet the same Vedas personified are called offensive and unqualified to live in Mayapur. How is that? He insists the audience must answer. — “Did you understand my question?”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:47 (auto-transcript): “I will ask you what you understand. What do you understand? Did you understand my question? Did you understand your question? What do you understand? What can you understand, baby? No, I will repeat a question. I will go to your question. Bhagavad Gita, 16, 23.”

Maharaj invites one contribution after another before giving his own answer, thanking each speaker.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:12 (auto-transcript): “Yes, okay. The interview was answering. Maharaj Ji, it's look Krishna playing with us. Hmm? It looks like Krishna is playing with us. Krishna is playing with us. Prabhu Ji is saying, I feel like Krishna is playing with us. Prabhu was speaking before. Chakandevas Prabhu Ji was…”

children.topic: A1 · Krishna is playing with us
children.note:
The first response: it looks like Krishna is playing with us.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:15 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj Ji, it's look Krishna playing with us. Hmm? It looks like Krishna is playing with us. Krishna is playing with us. Prabhu Ji is saying, I feel like Krishna is playing with us. Prabhu was speaking before. Chakandevas Prabhu Ji was saying something. Thank you. Thank you.…”

children.topic: A2 · The Vedas are a heartless process
children.note:
A devotee answers that the Vedas are a heartless process; Krishna wants a truthful relationship with the jiva. Rules and regulations purify, but one must reach the stage of bhakti to have a relationship with him and enter his realm.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:48 (auto-transcript): “um the vedas are a heartless process vedas are heartless process yes heartless krishna wants a truthful relationship with the soul with the jiva that's why you need the rules and regulations to purify yourself but ultimately you have to come to the perfectional stage of…”

Prabhupada's purport to 15.15 says the Vedas direct people back home; but the jnanis Mahaprabhu rejected see Krishna as formless — they have part of the Veda, not the complete Veda. Another devotee: they see a piece of the mountain, while Krishna, the knower of the Vedas, is the whole mountain. For dhama residents bhakti predominates and jnana stays second; for these people jnana covers bhakti.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:13 (auto-transcript): “In the 1515 Bhagavad Gita purport, Prabhupada was saying that Vedas give right direction to people so that they can mold their lives and come back home, back to Godhead. But here we see that Gyanis, whom Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was denying to live in Mayapur, they see Krishna as…”

They declare themselves knowers of the Vedas yet twist the Vedas' message; understanding by ourselves fails, only the spiritual master can throw light. Another adds: they have given up the essence and beat around the bush, and Mahaprabhu is the Supreme Person while they stop at Brahman.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:56 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, they are declaring themselves to be the knower of Vedas and at the same time they are twisting the messages of Vedas. What is their fault? They shouldn't twist the message from the Veda. Okay. if we try to understand by ourselves it is only the spiritual master can…”

children.topic: A5 · Progression, offense, the fifth goal
children.note:
Further contributions: the Gita trains Arjuna step by step from following dharma to leaving it, and Mahaprabhu completes that progression with bhakti; the jnanis crossed the ocean of the Vedas but offend the Lord and his devotees, reading Vasudeva impersonally though the Atharva Veda calls him Devaki-nandana; they speculate instead of following Krishna's own process; and in the Bhagavatam Narada rejects Vyasa's earlier literature in favour of prema, the fifth goal, which Mahaprabhu came to establish after Advaita Acarya saw jnanis spreading such ideas in Navadvipa.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:13 (auto-transcript): “Two minutes, so we can't close. So we see one more contradiction, like not contradiction but a progression. Like in the third chapter Krishna says that one who does not follow his dharma, he does not have good fortune neither in this life nor in the next. So he is encouraging…”

Vedas personified means the four Vedas, compiled for less qualified people to raise them to the human platform, so their teaching is material. Caitanya-caritamrta, Srimad-Bhagavatam and Bhagavad-gita are not included — they are the fifth Veda, and that is where Mahaprabhu speaks from.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:21 (auto-transcript): “Thank you Krishna, thank you all very much, we have beautiful contributions, all right, there are two things to look at, when we say Vedas personified does not include Shri Chaitanya Saritamrath Shri Matabhagwata Bhagavad Gita does not include looking at the four Vedas”

children.topic: Sukadeva: do not listen to the Vedas
children.note:
In the sixth canto Sukadeva Gosvami tells Pariksit Maharaj not to listen to the Vedas, because they misdirect the intelligence towards meaningless goals like going to heaven.

🎙 Maharaj at 71:38 (auto-transcript): “You see in the sixth scantum, Sukadev Goswami is telling Parikshit Maharaj. Don't listen to the Vedas. Because they will be misdirected to intelligence towards meaningless things like going to heaven. But what time you are not included. These are the fifth Vedas. So the…”

The four Vedas and the fifth Veda are not the same; they are separated. So there is no contradiction between Krishna compiling the Vedas and Mahaprabhu rejecting the Vedas personified. — “So Krishna is not contradicting himself.”

🎙 Maharaj at 72:22 (auto-transcript): “So the teaching, that is where Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is coming from. That's what I'm referring to. It's also within Ushri Jaya. He's coming from that side. to the two things here. Not the same. They are separated. So Krishna is not contradicting himself. I compiled Vedas.…”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 23 · What is Actual Liberation?

nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.148 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Out of millions of liberated souls a pure devotee is rare — and there are many levels even among pure devotees, illustrated by the Dhenukasura pastime. Maharaj asks what liberation actually is: not merely rising above the modes, but going back to Godhead, which comes by bhakti alone. The questions turn to who is in charge of a holy place, service versus position, and how nice chanting makes every other service devotional. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse sets out the rarity of a pure devotee of Krishna: among millions of wise men one is actually liberated, and among millions of such liberated persons a pure devotee is hard to find. Read with the Hindi translation and the English translation and purport.

Maharaj begins from the phrase 'a pure devotee is very difficult to find': there are many devotees, and they are not all on one level.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:40 (auto-transcript): “There are many devotees. There are many devotees. Many devotees. Canishtha devotees Madhyam devotees And Uttam devotees Within the Uttam Bhaktas Many categories”

The familiar three grades — neophyte, intermediate and topmost — and even within the uttama devotees there are many categories.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:52 (auto-transcript): “Canishtha devotees Madhyam devotees And Uttam devotees Within the Uttam Bhaktas Many categories Many categories Krishna is priya, sakhas, sakhis.”

In Goloka Krishna has sakhas and sakhis, priya-sakhas and priya-sakhis, and above them the priya-narma-sakhas and sakhis who are with him at every moment.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:32 (auto-transcript): “Krishna is priya, sakhas, sakhis. Yeah. Yeah, in Goloka, sakhas and sakhis. Priya, sakhis, priya, sakhas.”

Some associates see Krishna all day; others, though pure devotees — Maharaj names Nanda Maharaj — see him for less than that. Pure devotion still has levels, and some cowherd boys are even equal to Krishna in strength. — “Not only one category, different levels.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:57 (auto-transcript): “They see Krishna 24 hours. There are some who do not see Krishna 24 hours. Even though there are pure devotees. Or your Shodha. 24 hours. Nanda Maharaj. Less than 24.”

To show the different moods of Krishna's friends, Maharaj retells the killing of Dhenukasura at Talavana, not far from where the class is sitting.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:14 (auto-transcript): “When Krishna was physically here, then the cowhead boys told Krishna, not far from where we are standing. There is. At this particular time, they are fully ripe.”

children.topic: Ripe tala fruits nobody has tasted
children.note:
The cowherd boys tell Krishna and Balarama that the tala fruits nearby are fully ripe — can you smell them from here? For years no one has enjoyed them because the demon Dhenuka has made the grove his home. Maharaj adds that tala fruit needs skill to cook, or it turns bitter.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:29 (auto-transcript): “then the cowhead boys told Krishna, not far from where we are standing. There is. At this particular time, they are fully ripe. Have you eaten? You know how to cook it.”

children.topic: Why the boys do not go themselves
children.note:
Krishna and Balarama say: we are equal in strength, go and kill the demon yourselves. The boys reply that it is true, but Krishna and Balarama are kshatriyas — if they do it they will be glorified; we want you to have the credit.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:40 (auto-transcript): “Krishna and Balaram they told we are equal we have the same strength So you can go and kill the demon. What is the problem? Don't wait for us. Go and kill the demon. We have the same strength. The boy said, It is true. But, you are a shatriya.”

Krishna says a promise prevents him from acting, so Balarama goes with all the boys, who are delighted to finally eat the fruit. He encourages them to take as much as they like, and the brothers shake the trees so the fruit falls.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:51 (auto-transcript): “Krishna told Balaram I cannot do it because I have a promise you can take care so Balaram he went with all the boys The boys were very happy. After so many years, they are going to enjoy this fruit.”

Hearing the fruit fall, the demon comes to see. A demon cannot bear to see anyone happy; seeing the boys feasting, he is furious — this is my territory. — “The demon doesn't like to see anyone happy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:26 (auto-transcript): “Dhenuka Surah is going to see what is happening. And exactly what is happening. And when he saw Krishna Balaram and they cow head boys The demon doesn't like to see anyone happy. So they called it boys was happy. And enjoying the fruits. So Dhenu Kasur became very angry.”

children.topic: The pure fruit and the tainted fruit
children.note:
Balarama kills Dhenukasura and throws him into the trees. Fruit rains down, but the boys carefully take only what Balarama shook down and avoid the fruit tinted by the demon's blood. Krishna then deals with the demon's associates, and the grove is open to everyone in peace.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:50 (auto-transcript): “So Balaram took care of Denokasura. He caught him by the edge. I thought to do acrobatics. He caught him by the side. He caught his tongue. The spots. He caught the spot. He caught the top of the tree. All the trees broke down, all the fruit came down, but the boys were very…”

Maharaj stops the story to ask the room, more than once, whether we sometimes feel like Dhenukasura: I am in charge here, this place belongs to me, only my family and those loyal to me may come. Not always, he admits, but sometimes. — “Do we feel like that sometimes?”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:15 (auto-transcript): “This is my territory. Do we feel like that sometimes? Do you feel like that sometimes? I am in charge here. It is me here. Do we feel like that sometimes? Not always, but sometimes. Sometimes, not always. This place I am the one”

The point of the pastime for us: Krishna consciousness exists to break down this possessive, demonic mentality in the heart and bring the place and the person back to Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:39 (auto-transcript): “This is the soul of the dhenu and the Christian consciousness to dismantle this demonic vitality. and bring it to Krishna consciousness. The center of everything. Krishna is the tilak of the universe. Tilak. Krishna is the tilak of the universe. The fortune of Vrjibhasis.”

children.topic: Krishna is the tilak of the universe
children.note:
Krishna, not us, is the centre of everything — the tilak of the universe and the good fortune of the Vrajavasis and of all devotees. — “Krishna is the tilak of the universe.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:06 (auto-transcript): “The center of everything. Krishna is the tilak of the universe. Tilak. Krishna is the tilak of the universe. The fortune of Vrjibhasis. It's the fortune of devotees. So Krishna told the boy, Don't waste your time, wait. Don't disturb your enjoyment. Continue to eat, I will…”

Back to the purport: the jnanis, with their poor fund of knowledge, only think they are liberated. Maharaj asks the audience what liberation actually is.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:19 (auto-transcript): “So, different classes of devotees are there. Prabhupada said here, Srimad Bhagavatam 10.2.32, they said that due to their poor form of knowledge, the Gyanis are not actually liberated. So what is your liberation? The liberation is transcending the three modes of nature.”

children.topic: Beyond the modes is not enough
children.note:
The answer offered — transcending the three modes of nature — is incomplete. That alone is not real liberation.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:00 (auto-transcript): “The liberation is transcending the three modes of nature. So therefore, it is not actually a liberation. Depression naturally means to go back home, back to go ahead. That cannot be attained just by cultivating knowledge. By bhakti only. And one can achieve that.”

Actual liberation means going back home, back to Godhead. That cannot be reached by cultivating knowledge; only bhakti takes one there. — “By bhakti only.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:16 (auto-transcript): “Depression naturally means to go back home, back to go ahead. That cannot be attained just by cultivating knowledge. By bhakti only. And one can achieve that. Hare Krishna. Hare Krishna.”

A question from a mataji and a follow-up from a prabhu on who should be in charge if nobody owns anything.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:04 (auto-transcript): “Yes, ma'am. Hare Krishna. We see that in the material world, the exchanges will be very difficult if everyone starts thinking that I am not in charge, Krishna is in charge so anybody can come in anyone's house and then things will go chaotic very good so Prabhu Ji has a tip…”

children.topic: Q1 · No one in charge — chaos?
children.note:
If everyone in the material world thinks 'I am not in charge, Krishna is', anyone could walk into anyone's house. And in the dhama, how do we judge the one who says 'this is my place'? Maharaj calls it a very good point.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:14 (auto-transcript): “We see that in the material world, the exchanges will be very difficult if everyone starts thinking that I am not in charge, Krishna is in charge so anybody can come in anyone's house and then things will go chaotic very good so Prabhu Ji has a tip from a particular point…”

Maharaj parodies 'everything belongs to all of us — this computer is for all of us, no single person owns it'. That is not the teaching; it is capitalism in disguise. Somebody must be in charge. — “Somebody must be in charge.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:15 (auto-transcript): “Material communism. Material communism. Everything belongs to all of us. This computer is for all of us. This is for all of us. No single person owns it. It's for all of us.”

In our community the leader is Krishna. The servant leader is his representative, who manages everything but claims nothing for himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:37 (auto-transcript): “So in our community, spiritual communism, servant leader, not leader, but servant leader. Our leader is Krishna. Servant leader is a representative of Krishna. He does not claim anything. Right? See Srila Prabhupada,”

Srila Prabhupada established the institution, arranged everything, handed it to his disciples and left — Krishna in the centre, a body of devotees representing him. That is different from claiming it all and becoming attached to it.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:19 (auto-transcript): “See Srila Prabhupada, He established his condition, arranged everything, and gave to his disciples, and left spiritual communism. It is called to bring a samudayic body. Krishna is in the center. So we are representing Krishna. It is different from claiming everything.”

Maharaj widens the answer: once we think of ourselves as proprietors we lose sight of being devotees. What we hold is a service, not a position.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:16 (auto-transcript): “When we start to think of the proprietor, it is a service, not a position. How are we in a service, not a position?”

To think 'the position I have now is the proof of my devotion' is material. The real merit of a devotee is pure love of God, never a post. — “The merit of being a devotee is pure love of God.”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:05 (auto-transcript): “When we start to think, the position I have now, This is the merit of my being a devotee. Material. The merit of being a devotee is pure love of God. Not material position. It is a very dangerous mentality. When someone thinks, I am the proprietor.”

The proprietor mentality quickly becomes exploitation — since you are mine, I can use you as I like. Maharaj says this contamination has been choking the movement.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:45 (auto-transcript): “When someone thinks, I am the proprietor. It is a very dangerous mentality. We are starting to exploit the position. All of you are my property. It is a big contamination. So, since you are my property, I can use you as I like.”

Change a man's position and, if it was a position to him, he leaves the movement; if it was service, he stays. Sweeping here is service, cleaning the toilets is service, cooking is service — not only book distribution and college preaching.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:57 (auto-transcript): “If the position is changed, he will leave the movement. But if it is service, we will not leave the movement. Service is service. So, swooping here is service. Right? Swoping here is service. Not only book distribution. Not only college preaching. Not only needed the…”

Taking care of devotees is the best service — better than simply making new ones. Maharaj recalls Prabhupada's instruction to boil the milk rather than water it down.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:50 (auto-transcript): “Taking care of devotees is the best. My spiritual master said he was talking to his holiness Guru Prashad Swami Maharaj. He was telling my Gurudev, Bhakti Tita Maharaj, I want to make more devotees. My Gurudev said, I want to train the devotees you already met.”

children.topic: Gurudev: train the ones you already have
children.note:
Maharaj recounts an exchange between HH Guru Prasad Swami, who wanted to make more devotees, and his own Gurudev, HH Bhakti Tirtha Swami, who replied that he wanted to train the devotees already made. We have made many; how many are happy, satisfied, secure?

🎙 Maharaj at 35:58 (auto-transcript): “My spiritual master said he was talking to his holiness Guru Prashad Swami Maharaj. He was telling my Gurudev, Bhakti Tita Maharaj, I want to make more devotees. My Gurudev said, I want to train the devotees you already met. We have made so many devotees, We have met so many…”

Today we count disciples, congregation, properties and money. Maharaj calls all of these failures as measures. Real success is how many devotees have become purified — and with the 'you are my property' mentality we have no potency to purify anyone. — “All these things are failures.”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:37 (auto-transcript): “So today we are checking our success. How many disciples are there? How many congressmen are there in my temple? How many properties are there? How much money do you have? All these things are failures. All are failures. Success.”

Boiled milk means quality — go to the gosala and see. Quality means pure devotees. Speculation and self-importance are not bhakti; caring for devotees is how we actually progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:49 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupar told us. Boiled milk. We are boiling the milk. We are watering the milk. Shri Prabhupada says, Boiled milk. Boiled milk. That is required. Boiled milk means what? Boiled milk means what? Go to Gosala.”

Two further questions, on developing faith and on how other services support our chanting.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:51 (auto-transcript): “my question is how we can develop our faith is like that we can feel that krishna is always watching us and means how we can develop this faith and this consciousness”

children.topic: Q2 · Faith that Krishna is watching
children.note:
A devotee asks how to develop the faith and consciousness that Krishna is always watching us.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:51 (auto-transcript): “my question is how we can develop our faith is like that we can feel that krishna is always watching us and means how we can develop this faith and this consciousness”

Hear every day from bona fide sources and faith grows; chant and it improves; associate with faithful devotees and it increases. Maharaj stresses bona fide hearing — not just any hearing.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:36 (auto-transcript): “We should hear every day, every day, so here, bona fide hearing, if we hear, our Our faults will grow. If you chant. Our fate will increase and improve.”

Rupa Gosvami's Upadesamrta says the essence of all advice is to chant nicely. Maharaj presses the room: what do you consider nice chanting? Chanting while discussing, or while watching television? He rejects answers that only describe the result. — “What do you consider nice chanting?”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:57 (auto-transcript): “Rupa Goswami said, Shilarupa Goswami kehte hai, nice chanting. Ki Matr jab nahi karna hai, bohut achche se jab karna hai. Note of instruction? Upadesha Amrit mein, nice thing. What do you consider nice chanting? What is nice chanting? Please, listen to my question before you…”

Offenseless, attentive chanting is the result; Maharaj wants the practice that produces it. We cannot chant and hear while we keep grudges in the heart — if someone still sits negatively in the mind, we cannot really hear the name, whatever our 'bona fide reasons'.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:51 (auto-transcript): “What is attentive chanting? You are telling me the result. You are giving me the result. I am not asking for the result. I am asking the prati before you get the result. What is it? I understand. You understand? I am not asking for the result. You cannot eat before cooking.…”

children.topic: Q3 · How other services help chanting
children.note:
If ninety percent of our progress comes from chanting, how do the other services improve our sadhana and japa?

🎙 Maharaj at 48:18 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Mr. Maharaji, one more question. Maharaji, Prabhu said that our 90% progress in bhakti is due to chanting. And Maharaji, how the other service will help us to improve our sadhana and chanting? If you chant nicely,”

If we chant nicely our services become offerable; if we do not, they are not devotional. Everything else is added to support the chanting, since we cannot chant all day like Haridasa Thakura.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:46 (auto-transcript): “If you chant nicely, then our services will be offerable. if you don't chant nicely all of our services are not devotional”

children.topic: Deity worship added to purify us
children.note:
Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura added deity worship and many engagements to keep us protected and purified. These services are for our benefit; Krishna already has affectionate lovers serving him.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:43 (auto-transcript): “because we cannot do like Harid Ashtar Kaur Shra Jeeva Goswami Shra Bhakti Siddhanta Saraswati Thakura Mahupad added deity worship to our life to help us get purified all other services are added to support our chanting Because we cannot chant to draw out.”

children.topic: Service free of lust and pride
children.note:
Devotional service pleases Krishna only when it is not contaminated by lust and pride — 'I am the best distributor, nobody distributes books like me, I am the best speaker'. Many great distributors before us left the movement; we are not the first. — “Nobody can distribute books like me”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:46 (auto-transcript): “which gives Krishna pleasure but devourishment service not service contaminated by lust by pride I am the best distributor in this room I am the best Nobody can distribute books like me”

maps.title: Rupa Siksa · Day 24 · Pure and Selfless Desires of a Devotee

nodeData.topic: Day 24 · Pure and Selfless Desires of a Devotee
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.149 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Mahaprabhu tells Rupa Gosvami that only the devotee is peaceful, because he is nishkama; those who want enjoyment, liberation or mystic power stay restless. Maharaj walks through all four — the devotee's big but selfless desires, the bhukti mentality that even creeps into temple life, the dark peace of the jnani, and power as the strongest intoxicant — with Prabhupada's 'curse' to travel, Bill Gates, Hussain Shah, Banasura and a village yogi as examples. A long Q&A follows on preaching without being intoxicated by fame and on misuse of power within ISKCON. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse contrasts the devotee of Krishna, who is desireless and therefore peaceful, with the karmi, jnani and yogi, who all want something and so cannot be at peace. Maharaj says Mahaprabhu is teaching us how to do things properly so that we can be successful.

children.topic: Four people, four kinds of consciousness
children.note:
Krishna-bhakta, bhukti-kami, mukti-kami and siddhi-kami are in different situations because their consciousness is different. The devotee is shanta; the other three are not. Maharaj takes them one by one through the class.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:12 (auto-transcript): “Krishna Bhaktas, Bhuktis, Muktis, Siddhis, different situation because they have different consciousness. Krishna Bhakta is Santa. Krishna bhakti shant hota hai. Why? Nishkaam. No selfish desires.”

Nishkama does not mean no desires. To build a temple or a Vedic planetarium, or to preach around the whole world, is a very big desire — but it carries no reaction, because there is no selfishness in it.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:51 (auto-transcript): “No selfish desires. He has so many desires. Devotee. So many desires. To construct temple of Vedic pletarium is not a small desire, it's a big desire to preach around the world big desire not small desire very big desire”

Selfishness is not Krishna consciousness. The devotee is completely selfless and at the same time constantly looking for a chance to help humanity. — “The devotees are completely selfless, but they are very conscious about others' welfare.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:03 (auto-transcript): “As the nature of a devotee, free from material desires, selfishness is not Krishna consciousness. The devotees are completely selfless, but they are very conscious about others' welfare. Because they are constantly looking for the opportunity to help the humanity,”

Because the devotee lives for others' welfare, Krishna takes a personal interest in his life — and that is why he is free and happy.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:44 (auto-transcript): “Because they are constantly looking for the opportunity to help the humanity, Krishna will take personal interest in their life. Therefore, they are free and happy. But others are bhaktis those who are”

Those who want material enjoyment cannot be peaceful because they are separatists: their desires are centred on themselves and differ from Krishna's desire. They work very hard with big desires too, but the desire is sinful, while the devotee's desire is about Krishna and how to make Krishna consciousness easy for people.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:14 (auto-transcript): “But others are bhaktis those who are looking for material enjoyment. Bukhti, material enjoyment, they will not be peaceful. Because they are separatists. Their desires are different from Krishna's desire.”

The bhukti person's desire is self-centred, so he cannot be happy however hard he works; Krishna is always with the devotee because the devotee's desire is pure. — “Their desires are different from Krishna's desire.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:51 (auto-transcript): “Because they are separatists. Their desires are different from Krishna's desire. Centered within themselves. so they are selfish so they cannot be happy they work very hard big desires their desire is sinful but Krishna Bhakti's desire is pure in order about themselves”

The enjoyers also do not sleep, also work day and night, also travel all around. The travelling looks the same; the purpose is different, so the reaction is different. The devotee travels for the benefit of other living entities.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:09 (auto-transcript): “are also working hard they don't sleep as devotees are not sleeping the bhaktis also don't sleep they are working very hard day and night traveling all around pure devotees are traveling the bhakti is also traveling traveling is the same the purpose is different therefore the…”

Maharaj recalls Prabhupada saying that although he had palatial places all over the world he could not stay anywhere more than a few days, because there was a curse on his head — and that he wished to transfer this curse to his sannyasis so he could have time to translate Bhagavatam. One service given up only for another service; that is Krishna consciousness. — “Because I have a curse on my head.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:56 (auto-transcript): “proper said the parents of my disciples curse me. Even though I have nice palatial places around the world, I cannot stay there more than three days for one week. Because I have a curse on my head. But you know what Prabhupada said, I am looking for my sannyasis, so I can…”

children.topic: Do you want to follow Prabhupada?
children.note:
Maharaj asks the room repeatedly whether they want to take this hereditary karma: nice house, nice family, but you cannot stay — Germany, France, America, Japan, Africa. If you cannot do it, there is no advancement; if you want advancement, take the karma.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:53 (auto-transcript): “Do you want to follow Prabhupada? Do you want to follow Prabhupada? Want to guide the karma? It's hereditary karma, I say, hereditary karma. You stay in one place. You don't stay in one place. You travel. I pray Krishna consciousness. Want to do that?”

Without sacrifice one cannot be free or happy or please Krishna; it is the price to pay, and all our acaryas paid it. If we are followers we must do the same — not just read and speak and do nothing. Speech has value only when action follows. — “You cannot be free, you cannot be happy without sacrifice.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:16 (auto-transcript): “Where is this sacrifice? You cannot be free, you cannot be happy without sacrifice. Sacrifice is compulsory to please Krishna. It is compulsory. That is the price you have to pay. All our acharya did that. If we are followers, we have to do the same thing, don't just read and…”

People who do not know this travel the world, make money, even open free hospitals, schools and charitable foundations — all selfishness, and they are not happy. Maharaj says their charity is for expanding their own piety and enjoyment, not for anybody else, and the same holds for philanthropic societies.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:10 (auto-transcript): “people don't know this therefore they can travel around the world they can make money even open hospitals schools free charitable foundations all selfishness they would not be happy but they would not be what we see every day they are not happy Bill Gates has churchable…”

Bill Gates has a charitable foundation and millions of workers; he need only press a button and servants come with folded hands. Yet he suffers from loneliness, because nobody standing there is standing for him — stop paying them and they are gone. — “he is suffering from loneliness”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:38 (auto-transcript): “Bill Gates has churchable foundation, right? he is happy Bill Gates is happy suffering from loneliness loneliness We have millions of workers, he doesn't need to stand up, where he is sitting, just press a button, and thousands of servants will come, with the folded hands.…”

Seeing the crowds following Mahaprabhu, the king asked his minister who the sannyasi was. The minister, a devotee, played him down as a poor hungry mendicant. Hussain Shah replied: do not speak like that — if I stop paying, all my people leave, but this sannyasi pays nothing and they follow him completely; that is purity, and no one may disturb him in my kingdom.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:04 (auto-transcript): “That is the experience from Hussain Shah. When Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu came, he saw all the followers. He asked his minister Who is that Sanyasi? He is a devotee So he was afraid Because he is a demon He is asking for my Lord He is asking for my Lord So he will go and…”

According to our level of selflessness we influence people. Mahaprabhu, fully selfless and paying no one, draws millions every year — even animals, like bees to flowers. Even a demon could see it in his presence. — “He is attracting millions of people every year.”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:26 (auto-transcript): “So he is teaching us what he is doing, a devotee of Krishna, he is selfless and according to the level of our selflessness, that is how we are going to influence people, he is He is 100% self-level. He is attracting millions of people every year. Including animals. So, Bill…”

Pure devotees may lack worldly influence and be alone, yet they are fully satisfied and never lonely. The materialist has many people around him and is lonely, because nobody is there for him.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:18 (auto-transcript): “pure devotees are alone but not lonely others they have so many people they are lonely because no Buddhist is there for them. Aim for Buddhist is there for themselves. So they cannot be peaceful. They can have a philanthropic organization, society or charitable foundations.…”

Maharaj turns the lens on us: even in Hare Krishna temples he sees the enjoying mentality in how we treat people, and asks why the movement Prabhupada established as pure Krishna consciousness is being made material by us.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:26 (auto-transcript): “It's not for anybody. Even here in India, you see so many. Even in Hare Krishna temple also. There's a amount of kichdi we give the insult you get from it. You don't get the insult you get from it. The insult you get from it. Insult. A sensible person will not try. He will…”

children.topic: The insult over a plate of khichdi
children.note:
For a small quantity of khichdi the insult one receives is such that a sensible person will not even go for it; Maharaj says he avoids passing certain corners because it irritates him. Why so much insult? Look inside our hearts and see how dirty we are. — “Is Krishna treating us like that?”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:38 (auto-transcript): “There's a amount of kichdi we give the insult you get from it. You don't get the insult you get from it. The insult you get from it. Insult. A sensible person will not try. He will not go for it. Don't you see? Really, Hare Krishna temple, I've said. Hare Krishna temple. The…”

Treating people unkindly falls in the same bhukti category: my gratification, and I am ready to use you for it. Maharaj says he sees this everywhere, in how devotees mistreat each other — and that is why, instead of being happy, we are miserable.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:56 (auto-transcript): “The same thing is the same thing as Bukti. Treating people on kindly is within this cycle of Bukti. Treating people on kindly is within this Bukti category. Bukti. My gratification. I am ready to use you for my gratification. You see, see what devotees, you see how we are…”

children.topic: Why devotees leave the body lamenting
children.note:
Vrindavana dasa Thakura says in Caitanya-bhagavata that the seekers of bhukti, mukti and siddhi cannot leave their body peacefully, but the bhaktas do. Yet we see so-called bhaktas leaving the body in lamentation or anger. The cause is a whole life lived with the enjoying mentality. — “Bukti mentality, we have lived the whole of our life with Bukti mentality.”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:17 (auto-transcript): “You see, many devotees live in the body lamenting Why? What is happening for us? Devotees live in the body in anger Why? What is responsible for that? Bukti mentality, we have lived the whole of our life with Bukti mentality. The result is that we are not happy, the devotees…”

The jnanis, the mumukshus, want to merge out of sheer frustration — finish everything, no variety, no activity, and call that peace. Maharaj calls it being peaceful in darkness, and points to how miserable such people actually look.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:51 (auto-transcript): “the jjani jjani who are mumukshu the one who wants to be lean to do frustration because they are very frustrated to merge into Krishna and they finish everything no variety no activity and peaceful and my person”

children.topic: We want Krishna, not that peace
children.note:
Do you want that kind of peace? We are not interested in these things; we want Krishna, and when we have Krishna everything is complete.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:24 (auto-transcript): “see how miserable they are, but you want that kind of peace, you want that, we are not interested in these things, we want Krishna, when we have Krishna, everything is complete, yogis, siddhi, looking for mystic power, to become what? Sarabant No Second God And to be Second…”

The yogi wants mystic power in order to become a second God, and gets only trouble. Maharaj explains why power is more dangerous than any drink and illustrates it with Banasura and a yogi he knew of.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:44 (auto-transcript): “when we have Krishna, everything is complete, yogis, siddhi, looking for mystic power, to become what?
