Sarabant No Second God And to be Second God I am the second God but he will get nothing but just a tree just a tree and a tree will get It is one yogi It is one yogi It…”

Of all intoxicants alcohol is the mildest: drink too much and you become senseless and sleep. Power is far more intoxicating — the powerful man does not sleep, he stays very active looking for someone to control. — “looking for whom to control”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:43 (auto-transcript): “of all the intoxicants alcohol is the least This is the least intoxicant, the least intoxicant, there are other intoxicants, they are more dangerous than the other. Power, intoxicants. power intoxicants more intoxicating”

Having worshipped Shiva and received power, Banasura roamed everywhere hunting for an opponent, found none, and finally demanded that Shiva himself fight him. Shiva told him not to worry — someone would come. Krishna came, the Sudarshana cakra trimmed away his arms until only two were left, and only then, powerless, was he peaceful.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:51 (auto-transcript): “Don't forget it, Banasura, what did he do, Banasura, what did he do, Banasura, what was he doing, before fighting Krishna, he was worshipping Shiva, you should know our scriptures, Banasura I was looking for a person to fight with it. What is that? It's intoxication.”

The intoxication of power was such that Banasura offended the very guru who gave him the gift. Maharaj notes that our acaryas warned about this: like Jagai and Madhai forgetting Vaishnavas through drink, the power-intoxicated commit offences and are destroyed by it.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:15 (auto-transcript): “The power is destroying them. They will see, Vaisnavasa make offenses. he made offense to his own guru he made offense to his own guru he made offense to his own guru He said, come and fight with me. Shiv ji has given him a gift. But he has no difference. That's the level of…”

children.topic: The yogi who came to the city
children.note:
A yogi renounced everything, meditated in the forest and gained some mystic power. Having power, he had to use it, so he left the forest for the city and opened shop.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:57 (auto-transcript): “So this order yogi, after he got mystic power, what will he do? He will have to use it. So he left the forest. He came to the city. who goes to yogis mystics who goes to mystics who goes to them how do you call them yes yes all of them”

Maharaj asks who goes to mystics and gets the answer from the room: little people. Big people go to sadhus. The sadhu solves your karma; the mystic merely interferes with it. — “Big people will go to sadhus.”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:52 (auto-transcript): “Big people will go to sadhus. Little people will go to mystics. Right? To interfere with their karma. The sadhus will solve the karma. the misty world interfere with your karma so this man he came out”

He advertised cures — a child's problem, take this and it disappears — and a queue formed stretching to the bazaar. Those at the back feared the supply would run out before their turn, pressed forward and crushed him. His mystic power did not save him; that is how he died.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:31 (auto-transcript): “So people were coming There's a long queue So he's sitting here All the servants, the associates what do you want my business is working in this way a long queue from here to louis”

Three questions: how a preacher avoids being intoxicated by fame, what Maharaj makes of misuse of power inside ISKCON, and how newcomers are to be protected from being groomed by such people.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:55 (auto-transcript): “Is it true? as we are in a preaching moment and we are inspired for preaching and preaching is like is a blade as you said that when you get fame and power so how to maintain both like not getting fame and power or like not getting intoxicated by fame and power at the same…”

A devotee asks: preaching brings fame and power, which is a double-edged blade — how do we keep preaching and yet not get intoxicated? How does Maharaj himself do it?

🎙 Maharaj at 55:56 (auto-transcript): “as we are in a preaching moment and we are inspired for preaching and preaching is like is a blade as you said that when you get fame and power so how to maintain both like not getting fame and power or like not getting intoxicated by fame and power at the same time we have”

Our security is sadhana. If we practise nicely we become purified, and purity protects us — Maharaj points out that Prabhupada did not say philosophy is the force. — “so Prabhupada said purity is the force”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:11 (auto-transcript): “Our security. Or sadhana. So security. if we practice nicely we will be purified so Prabhupada said purity is the force it will protect us so we will do what is real bhakti”

Good sadhana lets us see ourselves as servants rather than as Swamis — not as a philosophical idea but as a lived fact — so that every day our understanding of Krishna consciousness improves in quality.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:50 (auto-transcript): “so we will do what is real bhakti we will see we will see ourselves as a servant, not Swami. If we see ourselves like that, not philosophical which is coming from good sadhana. Then we will do things nicely.”

Maharaj quotes a Vyasa-puja offering of Bhakti Tirtha Swami to Prabhupada: if I love you, I will use everything as service to you and will not claim my disciples or my position as my own. Such a mood comes from practice, not from philosophy alone. — “I will use them for you if I love you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:54 (auto-transcript): “He is the Solanus Bhaktitirtha Maharaj. One of his Vyasa Puja says to his Guru, he said, Dear Srila Prabhupada, if I love you, I will use everything as a service unto me. I will not claim my disciples my position as my own.”

children.topic: Remember your guru, or become one
children.note:
Philosophy lacks the potency to protect us that purity has. Always remember we walk under someone who is watching; Maharaj cites Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura's warning that if he did not remember his guru at every moment he would become the guru himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:50 (auto-transcript): “philosophy does not have the potency to protect us as much as purity which is the force so Prabhupada doesn't say philosophy is the force pure purity is the force So as we do our things nicely, always remember we are walking under someone who is watching”

children.topic: The book should be in us
children.note:
Speaking philosophy without practice leaves everything in the book and nothing in us; the work is not yet done. Success is when what the book says is found in us.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:31 (auto-transcript): “we are simply speaking philosophy without practice everything remains in a book not in us the work is not done yet what is said the book should be with us is success thank you for your amazing class maharaj i feel very fortunate i'm getting the chance to attend the house…”

children.topic: Q2 · Misuse of power within ISKCON
children.note:
A devotee who joined in 1994 asks, with apology, about leaders and even sannyasis who appear to do good sadhana yet use their position and disciples for self-aggrandisement, which seems to shake the movement's foundation. Maharaj says he is comfortable with the question.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:00 (auto-transcript): “is success thank you for your amazing class maharaj i feel very fortunate i'm getting the chance to attend the house program with your class so maharaj it seems like you touched on a very deep uh subject matter regarding um those who have power and how they may misuse their…”

Krishna had a purpose in giving the Gita and Prabhupada had a clear purpose in forming ISKCON — to make brahmanas out of sudras, with a method designed for it. The problem is that some come with no purpose, or with a different agenda, and so Prabhupada's purpose is not followed. — “But some of us who have come here have no purpose, no purpose.”

🎙 Maharaj at 65:32 (auto-transcript): “Lord Krishna has a purpose in giving us Bhagavad Gita. Do you know what? That's the purpose. Shila Prabhupada has the purpose of forming Iskon. And he made it very, very clear. I want to make brahmanas from sudras, very clear, and he designed his process, his method,”

children.topic: Krishna is more eager than we are
children.note:
Citing Prabhupada on Bhagavatam 1.2.17, Maharaj says Krishna is more eager to take us back home than we are to go. Yet many in this world do not want to go back — and such people, when they join, bring their own agendas and quietly feed their egos.

🎙 Maharaj at 67:08 (auto-transcript): “This afternoon, we are referring to a statement of Śrīla Prabhupāda. Canto 1, Chapter 17, Canto 1, Chapter 2, Text 17, Shri Mat Bhagavatam, Pahla Skand, Dousra Adhyay, Satraha Shloka, Shri La Prahupad says, Krishna is more eager to take all back home, back to Godhead than we…”

children.topic: Beads in hand is not chanting
children.note:
Do not assume everyone with a bead bag is chanting. Maharaj tells of a lady in the Mayapur Jagannatha temple sweeping dust onto his body while chanting, and of a devotee who greets a wealthy householder but ignores a sannyasi because his mood is material. That is not chanting.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:55 (auto-transcript): “So please, when you see someone with a bead eating, all of us are chanting, Please don't make mistake to a thing that all of us are changing. The King is sure. I'm seeing everybody. In Mayapur, Jagannath Mandir, I entered there one lady”

children.topic: Real chanting changes how we act
children.note:
If one chants nicely the intelligence, senses and heart are purified and one sees and acts properly; where that is missing, something is wrong. Prabhupada says that even without much intelligence, one fixed in service under a bona fide guru, society and scripture is guided by Krishna from within and becomes pure.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:47 (auto-transcript): “If she is chanting nicely, the intelligence will be purified. All the senses will be purified. The heart will be purified. He will see properly. He will act properly. if we don't see that then something is wrong this means something is wrong you get it?”

There are karma-yogis, speculating jnana-yogis and real bhaktas all inside this movement; do not expect a day when it holds only pure devotees. Maharaj's advice: look to your own practice to protect yourself, walk towards what you came for, and do not waste time on the others.

🎙 Maharaj at 75:05 (auto-transcript): “do you want me to tell something to you? so I tell you something please these people who remain in this movement did you hear me? these people who remain in this movement it's a main disappointment. Don't think that one day the woman had only pure devotees. Don't think like…”

children.topic: Q3 · Protecting newcomers from little empires
children.note:
The questioner presses on: preachers bring people in, but then some are groomed and whisked away into private followings, and new devotees cannot tell right from wrong. What is the solution?

🎙 Maharaj at 76:53 (auto-transcript): “i'm sorry i'm taking time my actual question yes maharaj you answered so deeply and beautifully but the concern really is that you know this movement is sending preachers they're bringing in people so people are coming but then they get misdirected and mistreated so i was…”

Innocent people come to the movement and someone inside, posing as a good devotee, guides them away. Maharaj names it plainly as a disservice. — “This is a disservice to the movement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 80:04 (auto-transcript): “They are, let's say, innocent people. They have come to their movement. And someone from inside pretending to be a good devotee”

If the newcomers are sincere they will come back after some time, without fail; Krishna knows our heart and responds accordingly. The serious find a serious person, and the insincere are matched with cheaters. Some wait millions of years for a pure devotee while never becoming pure themselves — one gets what one desires.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:07 (auto-transcript): “But I tell you the truth. If we are sincere followers, If they are safe for all of us, they will come back after some time. No mistake. Krishna knows our heart. He will respond accordingly. If we are serious, then we will go to a serious person. They are not seerals, Krishna…”
